questions.question: Identify 1/5 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 1/5 is of the form p/q with integers p = 1, q = 5 (q ≠ 0), so it is rational. Its decimal form 0.2 is terminating.

questions.question: Identify √2 / 8 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: √2 is irrational; dividing an irrational number by the non-zero rational number 8 leaves it irrational.

questions.question: Identify 5/√6 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: √6 is irrational, so 5/√6 (a non-zero rational over an irrational) is irrational.

questions.question: Identify 2/8 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 2/8 = 1/4 = 0.25, a terminating decimal, hence rational.

questions.question: Identify 1/√3 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: √3 is irrational; 1/√3 = √3/3 is also irrational.

questions.question: Identify √8 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: √8 = 2√2, and since √2 is irrational, √8 is irrational.

questions.question: Identify 0 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 0 can be written as 0/1, i.e. p/q form, so it is rational.

questions.question: Identify π as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: π = 3.14159... is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it cannot be written as p/q; it is irrational.

questions.question: Identify √5 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 5 is not a perfect square, so √5 = 2.236... is non-terminating non-recurring, hence irrational.

questions.question: Identify 22/3 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 22/3 is a ratio of two integers, so it is rational (22/3 = 7.333... recurring).

questions.question: Identify 1/π as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: π is irrational, so 1/π is also irrational.

questions.question: Identify 11/12 as a rational or irrational number.
questions.explanation: 11/12 = 0.91666... is a recurring decimal formed by a ratio of integers, so it is rational.

questions.question: Convert 5/8 into a decimal fraction and state whether it is terminating or non-terminating.
questions.explanation: Divide 5 by 8: 8 × 0.625 = 5 exactly, so the decimal ends after three places.

questions.question: Convert 4/18 into a decimal fraction and state its type.
questions.explanation: 4/18 simplifies to 2/9. Long division gives 0.222..., the digit 2 repeats for ever.

questions.question: Convert 1/15 into a decimal fraction and state its type.
questions.explanation: 1/15 = 0.0 then 6 repeats, giving 0.0666...

questions.question: Convert 49/8 into a decimal fraction and state its type.
questions.explanation: 49 ÷ 8 = 6.125 exactly, so the decimal terminates.

questions.question: Convert 207/15 into a decimal fraction and state its type.
questions.explanation: 207 ÷ 15 = 13.8 exactly (15 × 13.8 = 207).

questions.question: Convert 50/76 into a decimal fraction and state its type.
questions.explanation: 50/76 reduces to 25/38. The remainder never becomes zero and the digits repeat, so it is non-terminating recurring.

questions.question: Illustrate 8/10 on the number line.
questions.answer: 8/10 = 0.8, marked 8 small divisions to the right of 0 on a scale divided into tenths (between 0 and 1).
questions.explanation: Divide each unit interval into 10 equal parts; 8/10 lies at the 8th mark after 0.

questions.question: Illustrate −8/10 on the number line.
questions.answer: −8/10 = −0.8, marked 8 small divisions to the left of 0 (between −1 and 0).
questions.explanation: The negative sign places the point on the left of the origin at the 8th tenth.

questions.question: Illustrate 1¼ on the number line.
questions.answer: 1¼ = 1.25, marked between 1 and 2, one quarter of the way from 1.
questions.explanation: After 1, divide the next unit into 4 parts and take the 1st mark.

questions.question: Illustrate −1¼ on the number line.
questions.answer: −1¼ = −1.25, marked between −2 and −1, one quarter of the way from −1 towards −2.
questions.explanation: Symmetric to 1¼ on the negative side.

questions.question: Illustrate 2/3 on the number line.
questions.answer: 2/3 ≈ 0.67, marked between 0 and 1, two thirds of the way from 0.
questions.explanation: Divide the interval 0-1 into 3 equal parts; 2/3 is at the 2nd mark.

questions.question: Illustrate −2/3 on the number line.
questions.answer: −2/3 ≈ −0.67, marked between −1 and 0, two thirds of the way from 0 to the left.
questions.explanation: Symmetric to 2/3 on the negative side.

questions.question: Can you make a list of all real numbers between 1 and 2?
questions.answer: No. The real numbers between 1 and 2 form an infinite set (indeed uncountable); no complete list can be made.
questions.explanation: Between any two distinct real numbers there are infinitely many more, so a finite listing is impossible.

questions.question: Give a reason why π (π) is an irrational number.
questions.answer: Because its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it cannot be written in the form p/q.
questions.explanation: π = 3.14159265... never ends and never repeats a block of digits; every rational number has a terminating or recurring decimal, hence π is irrational.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: 5/7 is an example of an irrational number.
questions.explanation: 5/7 is a ratio of integers, so it is rational.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: π is an irrational number.
questions.explanation: π has a non-terminating non-recurring decimal expansion.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: 0.31591... is an example of a non-terminating and non-recurring decimal fraction.
questions.explanation: The digits continue without ending and without a repeating pattern, which is the decimal signature of an irrational number.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: 0.123 is an example of a recurring decimal fraction.
questions.explanation: 0.123 terminates, so it is not recurring.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: 1/3 and 2/3 are lying between 0 and 1.
questions.explanation: 1/3 ≈ 0.33 and 2/3 ≈ 0.67, both greater than 0 and less than 1.

questions.question: Tick the correct statement: 1/√3 is an example of a rational number.
questions.explanation: √3 is irrational, so 1/√3 is irrational.

questions.question: Name the property: 1/2 + 2/3 = 2/3 + 1/2.
questions.explanation: Changing the order of the addends does not change the sum: a + b = b + a.

questions.question: Name the property: 4/3 + (1/3 + 2/3) = (4/3 + 1/3) + 2/3.
questions.explanation: The grouping of addends does not change the sum: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c.

questions.question: Name the property: 9 × (10/9 + 20/9) = (9 × 10/9) + (9 × 20/9).
questions.answer: Left distributive property of multiplication over addition.
questions.explanation: a(b + c) = ab + ac: the 9 on the left multiplies each term inside the bracket.

questions.question: Name the property: (4/5 + 5/7) × 7/8 = (4/5 × 7/8) + (5/7 × 7/8).
questions.answer: Right distributive property of multiplication over addition.
questions.explanation: (b + c)a = ba + ca: the multiplier 7/8 is on the right.

questions.question: Name the property: (7/5 − 3/5) × 10/15 = (7/5 × 10/15) − (3/5 × 10/15).
questions.answer: Right distributive property of multiplication over subtraction.
questions.explanation: (b − c)a = ba − ca treats subtraction inside the bracket.

questions.question: Name the property: (d/c)(e/f) = (e/f)(d/c).
questions.explanation: The product is unchanged when the factors are interchanged: ab = ba.

questions.question: Name the property: 11 × (15 × 21) = (11 × 15) × 21.
questions.explanation: a(bc) = (ab)c: regrouping factors does not change the product.

questions.question: Name the property: (2/11) × (11/2) = (11/2) × (2/11) = 1.
questions.explanation: A number times its reciprocal equals 1: a × 1/a = 1.

questions.question: Name the property: (3/5) + (−3/5) = (−3/5) + (3/5) = 0.
questions.explanation: A number added to its negative gives the additive identity 0: a + (−a) = 0.

questions.question: Name the property: (a/b) × (b/a) = (b/a) × (a/b) = 1.
questions.explanation: The product of a number and its reciprocal is 1.

questions.question: Name the property: (15/10) × (8/5 − 4/10) = (15/10 × 8/5) − (15/10 × 4/10).
questions.answer: Left distributive property of multiplication over subtraction.
questions.explanation: a(b − c) = ab − ac.

questions.question: Name the property: (√2/3) × (3/√2) = (3/√2) × (√2/3) = 1.
questions.explanation: The two numbers are reciprocals, so their product is 1.

questions.question: Fill the box: √2/5 + 3/√6 = ☐/√6 + √2/5.
questions.explanation: By the commutative property of addition the terms are reordered, so the missing numerator is 3.

questions.question: Fill the boxes: 7/10 + (70/☐ + 16/33) = (7/10 + ☐) + 16/33.
questions.explanation: By the associative property the grouping shifts, so the inner denominator is 10 and the middle term stays 70/10.

questions.question: Fill the box: (99/50) × (50/99) = ☐.
questions.explanation: A number multiplied by its reciprocal equals the multiplicative identity 1.

questions.question: Fill the box: (59/95) × (95/59) = ☐.
questions.explanation: Reciprocals multiply to give 1.

questions.question: Fill the box: (−21) + (☐) = 0.
questions.explanation: The additive inverse of −21 is +21, since −21 + 21 = 0.

questions.question: Fill the boxes: (5/8)(2/3 + 5/7) = (☐ × 2/3) + (5/8 × ☐).
questions.explanation: Distributing the factor 5/8 over the bracket gives (5/8 × 2/3) + (5/8 × 5/7).

questions.question: Fill the blanks: 5 < 8 and 8 < 10 ⇒ ☐ < ☐.
questions.explanation: Transitive property of inequality: if a < b and b < c then a < c.

questions.question: Fill the blanks: 10 > 8 and 8 > 5 ⇒ ☐ > ☐.
questions.explanation: Transitive property: if a > b and b > c then a > c.

questions.question: Fill the blanks: 3 < 6 ⇒ 3 + 9 < ☐ + ☐.
questions.explanation: Added property of order: adding the same number to both sides keeps the inequality.

questions.question: Fill the blanks: 4 < 6 ⇒ 4 + 8 < ☐ + ☐.
questions.explanation: Adding 8 to both sides preserves 4 < 6.

questions.question: Fill the blanks: 8 > 6 ⇒ 6 + 8 > ☐ + ☐.
questions.explanation: Adding 6 to both sides of 8 > 6 gives 8 + 6 > 6 + 6, i.e. 6 + 8 > 6 + 6.

questions.question: Fill the blank: 5 < 7 ⇒ 5 × 12 < ☐ × ☐.
questions.explanation: Multiplying both sides by the positive number 12 keeps the inequality: 5 × 12 < 7 × 12.

questions.question: Fill the blank: 7 > 5 ⇒ 7 × 12 > ☐ × ☐.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the positive number 12 preserves 7 > 5.

questions.question: Fill the blank: 6 > 4 ⇒ 6 × (−7) ☐ 4 × (−7).
questions.answer: < (six times −7 is less than four times −7).
questions.explanation: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses it: −42 < −28.

questions.question: Fill the blank: 2 < 8 ⇒ 2 × (−4) ☐ 8 × (−4).
questions.explanation: Multiplication by a negative reverses the inequality.

questions.question: Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of 3.
questions.explanation: 3 + (−3) = 0 and 3 × 1/3 = 1.

questions.question: Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of −7.
questions.explanation: −7 + 7 = 0 and −7 × (−1/7) = 1.

questions.question: Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of 0.3.
Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of −√5/5.
questions.explanation: Negating gives the additive inverse; flipping gives the reciprocal −5/√5 = −√5.

questions.question: Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of 9/√12.
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of 9/√12 is √12/9 (= 2√3/9).

questions.question: Find the additive and multiplicative inverse of 0.
questions.answer: Additive inverse = 0; multiplicative inverse does not exist.
questions.explanation: 0 + 0 = 0, but no number multiplied by 0 gives 1, so 0 has no reciprocal.

questions.question: Identify the radicand and index in ∛5.
questions.explanation: In ⁿ√a, "a" is the radicand and "n" the index of the root.

questions.question: Identify the radicand and index in ⁴√(x/y).
questions.explanation: The expression under the radical sign is the radicand; the small number is the index.

questions.question: Identify the radicand and index in ⁵√(x²yz).
questions.explanation: Everything inside the radical is the radicand.

questions.question: Identify the radicand and index in √(ab).
questions.explanation: A square root has the implied index 2.

questions.question: Identify the radicand and index in ⁿ√(pq/r).
questions.explanation: The radicand is the fraction pq/r and the index is the nth root.

questions.question: Transform √(3/4) into exponential form.
Transform √((x/y)⁵) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: The square root gives power 1/2, which multiplies the existing power 5.

questions.question: Transform ∛((y/x)^(−5)) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Cube root = power 1/3, multiplied by −5.

questions.question: Transform ∛((yz)⁷) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Cube root of a 7th power = power 7/3.

questions.question: Transform ⁵√27 into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Ninth root => power 1/9.

questions.question: Transform ∛((−64)²) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Cube root of the square => power 2/3.

questions.question: Transform ∛((1/2)^m) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Cube root multiplies the exponent by 1/3.

questions.question: Transform ⁵√((xy)³) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Fifth root of a cube => power 3/5.

questions.question: Transform ∛(4/3) into exponential form.
questions.explanation: Cube root => power 1/3.

questions.question: Transform (5³)^(1/7) into radical form.
questions.explanation: A fractional power 1/7 becomes the seventh root.

questions.question: Transform (ab^(−2))^(1/3) into radical form.
questions.explanation: The cube root places ab^(−2) = a/b² under the radical.

questions.question: Transform [(5/7)³]^(5/7) into radical form.
questions.explanation: Multiplying exponents 3 × 5 gives 15, and the 7th root is taken.

questions.question: Transform (b/a)^(−m/2) into radical form.
questions.explanation: The negative exponent inverts the base and the 1/2 power becomes a square root.

questions.question: Transform [(11/13)(12/13)]^(1/5) into radical form.
questions.explanation: The 1/5 power gives the fifth root of the product.

questions.question: Simplify 3⁵ / 3².
questions.explanation: Law of quotient of powers: aᵏ/aⁿ = a^(m−n); 5 − 2 = 3.

questions.question: Simplify (2⁴ · 5³) / 10².
Simplify [(a+b)²(c+d)³] / [(a+b)(c+d)²].
questions.explanation: Subtract exponents of like bases: (a+b)^(2−1) (c+d)^(3−2).

questions.question: Simplify (1/3)⁴ × (1/3)⁵.
questions.explanation: Law of product of powers: add exponents 4 + 5 = 9.

questions.question: Simplify (3/4)⁵ × (3/4)².
questions.explanation: Add exponents 5 + 2 = 7.

questions.question: Simplify (−4/5)³ × (−4/5)⁵.
questions.explanation: Add exponents 3 + 5 = 8; an even power removes the minus sign.

questions.question: Simplify (−3 × 5²)³.
questions.explanation: Inside: −3 × 25 = −75; (−75)³ = −421875.

questions.question: Simplify [3 × (−4)²]³.
Simplify (−a/bc)⁵ × (−a/bc)⁴.
questions.explanation: Add exponents 5 + 4 = 9; an odd power keeps the minus sign.

questions.question: Simplify (−c/d)²(−c/d)³(−c/d)⁵.
questions.explanation: Add exponents 2 + 3 + 5 = 10; even power removes the minus sign.

questions.question: Simplify m²t⁴n³m³t⁵l⁷.
questions.explanation: Add the exponents of each base: m: 2+3 = 5; t: 4+5 = 9; n: 3; l: 7.

questions.question: Simplify a²c⁵b²a³c³b⁴a⁴.
questions.explanation: Add exponents per base: a: 2+3+4 = 9; b: 2+4 = 6; c: 5+3 = 8.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: (5²)³.
questions.explanation: Law of power of a power: multiply exponents 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(xy)³]⁵.
questions.explanation: Multiply exponents 3 × 5 = 15 and distribute over the product.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(−4)²]⁵.
questions.explanation: Multiply exponents 2 × 5 = 10; the even power makes the result positive.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(−3)³(−4)²]³.
questions.explanation: Inside: (−27)(16) = −432; (−432)³ = −80621568.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: (b²/5)³.
questions.explanation: Law of power of a quotient: (a/b)ⁿ = aⁿ/bⁿ.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(−4/9)²]³.
questions.explanation: Multiply exponents 2 × 3 = 6; the even power is positive.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(z³)²]⁴.
questions.explanation: Multiply exponents 3 × 2 × 4 = 24.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: [(m·m²·m³·m⁴)²]⁵.
questions.explanation: Inside bracket: m^(1+2+3+4) = m^10; then m^(10×2×5) = m^100.

questions.question: Simplify using the law of exponents: −[(−0.1)²(−0.1)³(−0.1)⁴]².
questions.explanation: Inside bracket: (−0.1)^(2+3+4) = (−0.1)^9 = −10^(−9); squaring gives 10^(−18); the leading minus makes it −10^(−18).

questions.question: Write (1, 2) in the form a + ib.
questions.explanation: The ordered pair (a, b) corresponds to a + ib.

questions.question: Write (2, 2) in the form a + ib.
questions.explanation: First entry is the real part, second the imaginary part.

questions.question: Write (0, 4) in the form a + ib.
questions.explanation: A zero real part leaves a pure imaginary number.

questions.question: Write (−1, 1) in the form a + ib.
Write (−2, 0) in the form a + ib.
questions.explanation: A zero imaginary part leaves a real number.

questions.question: Write (−3, 4) in the form a + ib.
Find the real and imaginary parts of 1 + 2i.
questions.explanation: In z = a + ib, a is the real and b the imaginary part.

questions.question: Find the real and imaginary parts of 9i + 4.
questions.explanation: Rewrite as 4 + 9i.

questions.question: Find the real and imaginary parts of (−5, 6).
questions.explanation: The pair (a, b) gives a = −5, b = 6.

questions.question: Find the real and imaginary parts of −1 − i.
Find the real and imaginary parts of (−3/4) − (−4/5)i.
questions.explanation: The coefficient of i is −(−4/5) = 4/5.

questions.question: Find the real and imaginary parts of 2i − 1.
questions.explanation: Rewrite as −1 + 2i.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of 3 + 2i.
questions.explanation: Change the sign of the imaginary part.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (0, −7).
questions.explanation: Negating the imaginary component gives (0, 7).

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (−1, 0).
questions.explanation: A real number is its own conjugate.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of 1 − i.
Find the conjugate of (−3/4) + (−4/5)i.
questions.explanation: The imaginary part changes sign.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of 3i + 1.
questions.explanation: Write as 1 + 3i and negate the imaginary part.

questions.question: Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of (4/7) + (9/10)i equals the number itself.
questions.answer: (4/7) − (9/10)i is the conjugate; its conjugate is (4/7) + (9/10)i, which equals the given number.
questions.explanation: Applying conjugation twice restores the original sign of the imaginary part.

questions.question: Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of (−9/11) + (10/9)i equals the number itself.
questions.explanation: Double conjugation leaves the number unchanged.

questions.question: Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of 1/2 − 3i equals the number itself.
questions.explanation: Double conjugation is the identity operation.

questions.question: Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of 2 + 3i equals the number itself.
Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of −2 − 3(−10/9)i equals the number itself.
questions.answer: The number is −2 + (10/3)i; conjugate −2 − (10/3)i; conjugate again returns −2 + (10/3)i.

questions.question: Verify that the conjugate of the conjugate of 4x + 3iy equals the number itself.
Find x and y if x + yi = −5 + 5i.
questions.explanation: Equate real and imaginary parts of equal complex numbers.

questions.question: Find x and y if x² + iy² = 16/9 + (9/25)i.
questions.explanation: x² = 16/9 so x = ±4/3; y² = 9/25 so y = ±3/5.

questions.question: Find x and y if y² + (x/3)i = 121 − (9/5)i.
questions.explanation: y² = 121 => y = ±11; x/3 = −9/5 => x = −27/5.

questions.question: Find x and y if (√5/3)x − (3/√2)yi = 6√3/√2 + (2√2/9)i.
questions.explanation: Equate real parts: (√5/3)x = 6√3/√2 = 3√6 gives x = 9√6/√5. Equate imaginary parts: −(3/√2)y = 2√2/9 gives y = −4/27.

questions.question: Perform the operation: (3, 2) + (9, 3).
Perform the operation: (3/2, 2/3) + (2/3, 3/2).
Perform the operation: (15, 12) − (10, −9).
questions.explanation: (a−c, b−d) = (15−10, 12−(−9)).

questions.question: Perform the operation: (4/5, 8/15) − (4/5, 6/10).
Perform the operation: (1, 2)(1, −2).
questions.explanation: (a,b)(c,d) = (ac−bd, ad+bc) = (1+4, −2+2).

questions.question: Perform the operation: (4, −5)(5, −4).
questions.explanation: (4×5 − (−5)(−4), 4×(−4) + (−5)(5)) = (20−20, −16−25).

questions.question: Perform the operation: (3, −7) ÷ (3, 2).
questions.explanation: ((ac+bd)/(c²+d²), (bc−ad)/(c²+d²)) with a=3,b=−7,c=3,d=2: ((9−14)/13, (−21−6)/13).

questions.question: Perform the operation: (4, 5) ÷ (2, −3).
Simplify and write in the form a + ib: −1/(1+i).
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1−i): −(1−i)/2.

questions.question: Simplify and write in the form a + ib: (1+i)⁴.
Simplify and write in the form a + ib: (1/(1+i))².
questions.explanation: 1/(1+i) = (1−i)/2; squaring gives (1−i)²/4 = (−2i)/4 = −i/2.

questions.question: Simplify and write in the form a + ib: (1+i)⁸.
If z₁ = −4 + 6i and z₂ = 5/2 − 2i, verify that the conjugate of (z₁ + z₂) = conjugate of z₁ + conjugate of z₂.
questions.answer: Both sides equal −3/2 − 4i, so the identity holds.
questions.explanation: z₁ + z₂ = −3/2 + 4i, whose conjugate is −3/2 − 4i; the sum of conjugates is the same.

questions.question: If z₁ = −4 + 6i and z₂ = 5/2 − 2i, verify that the conjugate of (z₁ − z₂) = conjugate of z₁ − conjugate of z₂.
questions.explanation: z₁ − z₂ = −13/2 + 8i; its conjugate is −13/2 − 8i, matching the difference of conjugates.

questions.question: If z₁ = 1 + i and z₂ = 1 − i, verify that the conjugate of z₁z₂ = conjugate(z₁) · conjugate(z₂).
questions.explanation: z₁z₂ = (1+i)(1−i) = 2; conjugates multiply to (1−i)(1+i) = 2.

questions.question: If z₁ = 1 + i and z₂ = 1 − i, verify that the conjugate of z₁/z₂ = conjugate(z₁)/conjugate(z₂).
questions.explanation: z₁/z₂ = i, conjugate −i; conjugate ratio = (1−i)/(1+i) = −i.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Multiplicative inverse of √5 is ______.
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of √5 multiplied by √5 gives 1.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Q ∪ Q′ = ______.
questions.explanation: The union of the rationals and the irrationals is the set of real numbers.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The additive identity in R is ______.
questions.explanation: a + 0 = a for every real number a.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 5 + (6 + 7) = (5 + 6) + ______.
questions.explanation: Associative property of addition.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 3 + (−3) = ______.
questions.explanation: A number plus its additive inverse is zero.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: π is a ______ number.
questions.explanation: π has a non-terminating non-recurring decimal.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 22/7 is a ______ number.
questions.explanation: 22/7 is a ratio of two integers.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The conjugate of −3 + 5i is ______.
questions.explanation: Change the sign of the imaginary part.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In 2i(3 − i), the real part is ______.
questions.explanation: 2i(3 − i) = 6i − 2i² = 6i + 2 = 2 + 6i, so Re = 2.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The product of two complex numbers (a, b) and (c, d), i.e. (a,b)·(c,d) = ______.
questions.explanation: This is the multiplication rule in ordered-pair form.

questions.question: True/False: R is closed under multiplication.
questions.explanation: The product of any two real numbers is again real.

questions.question: True/False: If x < y and y < z then x < z.
questions.explanation: Transitive property of order.

questions.question: True/False: For all x, y, z in R, x(y − z) = xy − xz.
questions.explanation: Distributive property of multiplication over subtraction.

questions.question: True/False: The product of every two imaginary numbers is real.
questions.explanation: If z₁ = bi and z₂ = di then z₁z₂ = bdi² = −bd, a real number.

questions.question: Write 7<sup>3</sup> = 343 in logarithmic form.
questions.explanation: By definition, if a<sup>x</sup> = y then x = log<sub>a</sub> y. Here a = 7, x = 3, y = 343.

questions.question: Write 3<sup>−4</sup> = 1/81 in logarithmic form.
questions.explanation: Using a<sup>x</sup> = y ⇔ x = log<sub>a</sub> y with a = 3, x = −4, y = 1/81.

questions.question: Write 10<sup>−3</sup> = 0.001 in logarithmic form.
questions.explanation: Here a = 10, x = −3, y = 0.001, so log<sub>10</sub> 0.001 = −3.

questions.question: Write ∛(8<sup>2</sup>) = 4 in logarithmic form.
Write log<sub>27</sub> 81 = 4/3 in exponential form.
questions.explanation: From log<sub>a</sub> y = x we have a<sup>x</sup> = y, so (27)<sup>4/3</sup> = 81.

questions.question: Write log<sub>2</sub> (1/8) = −3 in exponential form.
questions.explanation: Using a<sup>x</sup> = y with a = 2, x = −3, y = 1/8.

questions.question: Write log<sub>10</sub> 1 = 0 in exponential form.
questions.explanation: Any non-zero base raised to the power 0 equals 1, so 10<sup>0</sup> = 1.

questions.question: Write log<sub>10</sub> (0.01) = −2 in exponential form.
questions.explanation: Here a = 10, x = −2, y = 0.01, giving 10<sup>−2</sup> = 0.01.

questions.question: Find x if log<sub>32</sub> x = 1/2.
questions.explanation: log<sub>32</sub> x = 1/2 ⇒ x = 32<sup>1/2</sup> = √32 = 4√2.

questions.question: Find a if log<sub>a</sub> 3 = 1/2.
questions.explanation: log<sub>a</sub> 3 = 1/2 ⇒ a<sup>1/2</sup> = 3 ⇒ a = 3<sup>2</sup> = 9.

questions.question: Find y if log<sub>√5</sub> 25 = y.
questions.explanation: log<sub>√5</sub> 25 = y ⇒ (√5)<sup>y</sup> = 25 ⇒ 5<sup>y/2</sup> = 5<sup>2</sup> ⇒ y/2 = 2 ⇒ y = 4.

questions.question: Find x if log<sub>4</sub> x = 3/2.
questions.explanation: log<sub>4</sub> x = 3/2 ⇒ x = 4<sup>3/2</sup> = (2<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3/2</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup> = 8.

questions.question: Find y if log<sub>10</sub> 100 = y.
questions.explanation: log<sub>10</sub> 100 = y ⇒ 10<sup>y</sup> = 100 = 10<sup>2</sup> ⇒ y = 2.

questions.question: Find a if log<sub>a</sub> 64 = 3.
questions.explanation: log<sub>a</sub> 64 = 3 ⇒ a<sup>3</sup> = 64 = 4<sup>3</sup> ⇒ a = 4.

questions.question: Find a if log<sub>a</sub> 1 = 0.
questions.answer: a is any positive real number (a > 0, a ≠ 1)
questions.explanation: For every admissible base a, a<sup>0</sup> = 1, so log<sub>a</sub> 1 = 0 holds for all positive a ≠ 1.

questions.question: Find y if log<sub>55</sub> 55 = y.
questions.explanation: log<sub>55</sub> 55 = y ⇒ 55<sup>y</sup> = 55<sup>1</sup> ⇒ y = 1.

questions.question: Find x if log<sub>64</sub> 8 = x/2.
questions.explanation: log<sub>64</sub> 8 = x/2 ⇒ 64<sup>x/2</sup> = 8 ⇒ (2<sup>6</sup>)<sup>x/2</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup> ⇒ 2<sup>3x</sup> = 2<sup>3</sup> ⇒ 3x = 3 ⇒ x = 1.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 8.
questions.explanation: 8 = 8.0 × 10<sup>0</sup>, so the characteristic is 0. From the log table, log of 8000 is 0.9031, so the mantissa is 0.9031.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 5054.
questions.explanation: 5054 = 5.054 × 10<sup>3</sup>, so the characteristic is 3. The mantissa from the log table (row 50, col 5, mean diff 4) is 0.7036.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 9.992.
questions.explanation: 9.992 = 9.992 × 10<sup>0</sup>, so the characteristic is 0. Rounding to 4 digits (9992), the mantissa is 0.9997.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 765.3.
questions.explanation: 765.3 = 7.653 × 10<sup>2</sup>, so the characteristic is 2. The mantissa from the table (7653) is 0.8839.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 0.00329.
questions.explanation: 0.00329 = 3.29 × 10<sup>−3</sup>, so the characteristic is −3. The mantissa from the table (3290) is 0.5172.

questions.question: Find the characteristic and mantissa of the logarithm of 0.0000300.
questions.explanation: 0.0000300 = 3.00 × 10<sup>−5</sup>, so the characteristic is −5. The mantissa from the table (3000) is 0.4771.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 9.
questions.explanation: 9 = 9.0 × 10<sup>0</sup>, characteristic 0. Mantissa of 9000 from the table is 0.9542, so log 9 = 0.9542.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 55.56.
questions.explanation: 55.56 = 5.556 × 10<sup>1</sup>, characteristic 1. Mantissa of 5556 is 0.7448, so log 55.56 = 1.7448.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 29.592.
questions.explanation: 29.592 = 2.9592 × 10<sup>1</sup>, characteristic 1. Mantissa of 2959 (rounded, mean diff 2) is 0.4711, so log = 1.4711.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 405.3.
questions.explanation: 405.3 = 4.053 × 10<sup>2</sup>, characteristic 2. Mantissa of 4053 is 0.6078, so log = 2.6078.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 0.00469.
questions.explanation: 0.00469 = 4.69 × 10<sup>−3</sup>, characteristic −3. Mantissa of 4690 is 0.6712, so log = −3 + 0.6712 = 3̄.6712.

questions.question: Find the logarithm of 0.000076.
questions.explanation: 0.000076 = 7.6 × 10<sup>−5</sup>, characteristic −5. Mantissa of 7600 is 0.8808, so log = −5 + 0.8808 = 5̄.8808.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 3.109 without using the log table.
questions.explanation: The digits are the same, so the mantissa is unchanged (0.4926). 3.109 has characteristic 0, so log 3.109 = 0.4926.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 310.9 without the table.
questions.explanation: 310.9 = 3.109 × 10<sup>2</sup>, so the characteristic is 2 and log 310.9 = 2.4926.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 0.003109 without the table.
questions.explanation: 0.003109 = 3.109 × 10<sup>−3</sup>, so the characteristic is −3 and log = −3 + 0.4926 = 3̄.4926.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 3109 without the table.
questions.explanation: 3109 = 3.109 × 10<sup>3</sup>, so the characteristic is 3 and log 3109 = 3.4926.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 310.942 without the table.
questions.explanation: The significant digits 3109.. are the same, characteristic 2, so log 310.942 = 2.4926.

questions.question: Given log 31.09 = 1.4926, find log 310926 without the table.
questions.explanation: 310926 = 3.10926 × 10<sup>5</sup>, so the characteristic is 5 and log 310926 = 5.4926.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 3.56721.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 3 ⇒ 4 digits. Mantissa .5672 → antilog (row .56, col 7) = 3698, mean diff 2 → +2 = 3700... using the given key the number is 3692.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 1.7427.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 1 ⇒ 2 digits before the point. Antilog of .7427 is 5530, so the number is 5.530 × 10<sup>−1</sup> = 0.5530.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 0.35749.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 0 ⇒ 1 digit before the point. Antilog of .35749 is 2278, giving 2.278.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 5.8196.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 5 ⇒ 6 digits. Antilog of .8196 is 6607 (approx.) giving the value 653800 as per the table.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 4.3847.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 4 is treated with the bar so the result is less than 1; antilog of .3847 is 2425, giving 2.425 × 10<sup>−4</sup> = 0.0002425.

questions.question: By using table, find the number whose common logarithm is 0.9187.
questions.explanation: Characteristic 0 ⇒ 1 digit before the point. Antilog of .9187 is 8292, giving 8.292.

Express log<sub>a</sub> (xyz) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y + log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: Product law: the log of a product equals the sum of the logs.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (x<sup>2</sup>y) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.explanation: Product law plus power law: log<sub>a</sub>(x<sup>2</sup>y) = log<sub>a</sub> x<sup>2</sup> + log<sub>a</sub> y = 2 log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (xy/z) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y − log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: Product and quotient laws: log<sub>a</sub>(xy) − log<sub>a</sub> z = log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y − log<sub>a</sub> z.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> √(xy) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.explanation: √(xy) = (xy)<sup>1/2</sup>, so log<sub>a</sub>(xy)<sup>1/2</sup> = ½(log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y).

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (1/√(xyz)) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: −½ log<sub>a</sub> x − ½ log<sub>a</sub> y − ½ log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: (xyz)<sup>−1/2</sup> gives −½(log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y + log<sub>a</sub> z).

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (x<sup>3</sup>y/z<sup>2</sup>) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: 3 log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y − 2 log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: Expand: 3 log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y − 2 log<sub>a</sub> z.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> √(xy<sup>2</sup>z) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: ½ log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y + ½ log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: √(xy<sup>2</sup>z) = (xy<sup>2</sup>z)<sup>1/2</sup>, so ½(log<sub>a</sub> x + 2 log<sub>a</sub> y + log<sub>a</sub> z) = ½ log<sub>a</sub> x + log<sub>a</sub> y + ½ log<sub>a</sub> z.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (∛(x<sup>−1</sup>√(y<sup>3</sup>)) ÷ √(y<sup>3</sup>√x)) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.explanation: Numerator = x<sup>−1/3</sup> y<sup>1/2</sup>, denominator = y<sup>3/2</sup> x<sup>1/4</sup>. Quotient = x<sup>−1/3−1/4</sup> y<sup>1/2−3/2</sup> = x<sup>−7/12</sup> y<sup>−1</sup>, giving −7/12 log<sub>a</sub> x − log<sub>a</sub> y.

questions.question: Express log<sub>a</sub> (x√(y<sup>3</sup>) / ∛(z<sup>2</sup>x<sup>5</sup>)) in terms of log<sub>a</sub> x, log<sub>a</sub> y and log<sub>a</sub> z.
questions.answer: −2/3 log<sub>a</sub> x + 3/2 log<sub>a</sub> y − 2/3 log<sub>a</sub> z
questions.explanation: Numerator = x y<sup>3/2</sup>, denominator = z<sup>2/3</sup> x<sup>5/3</sup>. Ratio = x<sup>1−5/3</sup> y<sup>3/2</sup> z<sup>−2/3</sup> = x<sup>−2/3</sup> y<sup>3/2</sup> z<sup>−2/3</sup>.

questions.question: Reduce log<sub>a</sub> 20 − log<sub>a</sub> 15 + ½ log<sub>a</sub> (9/2) to a single term.
questions.explanation: ½ log<sub>a</sub>(9/2) = log<sub>a</sub>√(9/2) = log<sub>a</sub>(3/√2). Then log<sub>a</sub>(20/15 × 3/√2) = log<sub>a</sub>(4/√2) = log<sub>a</sub>(2√2).

questions.question: Reduce (1/3) log<sub>a</sub>(x−1)<sup>3</sup> + (10/9) log<sub>a</sub>(x+1) − (1/9) log<sub>a</sub>(x+1) to a single term.
questions.explanation: (1/3)log<sub>a</sub>(x−1)<sup>3</sup> = log<sub>a</sub>(x−1). The last two terms combine to log<sub>a</sub>(x+1). So log<sub>a</sub>[(x−1)(x+1)] = log<sub>a</sub>(x<sup>2</sup>−1).

questions.question: Reduce log x − 2 log x + 3 log(x+1) − log(x<sup>2</sup>−1) to a single term.
questions.explanation: log x − 2 log x = −log x. And log(x<sup>2</sup>−1) = log(x−1)+log(x+1). So 3log(x+1) − log(x−1) − log(x+1) − log x = log[(x+1)<sup>2</sup>/(x(x−1))].

questions.question: If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log 15 without tables.
If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log 64 without tables.
If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log √(5 × 2) without tables.
questions.explanation: log √(5×2) = log √10 = ½ log 10 = ½ × 1 = 0.5.

questions.question: If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log 48 without tables.
If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log √18 without tables.

If log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771 and log 5 = 0.6990, find log (8/3) without tables.

Prove that log<sub>b</sub> m × log<sub>m</sub> a = log<sub>b</sub> a.
questions.explanation: Write log<sub>m</sub> a = log<sub>b</sub> a / log<sub>b</sub> m (change of base). Multiplying by log<sub>b</sub> m gives log<sub>b</sub> a. Hence proved.

questions.question: Prove that log<sub>a</sub> b × log<sub>c</sub> a = log<sub>c</sub> b.
questions.explanation: log<sub>c</sub> a = log<sub>a</sub> a / log<sub>a</sub> c = 1/log<sub>a</sub> c. Then log<sub>a</sub> b × log<sub>c</sub> a = log<sub>a</sub> b / log<sub>a</sub> c = log<sub>c</sub> b. Hence proved.

questions.question: Prove that log<sub>b</sub> a × log<sub>c</sub> b × (1/log<sub>c</sub> a) = 1.
questions.explanation: log<sub>c</sub> b = log<sub>a</sub> b / log<sub>a</sub> c and log<sub>b</sub> a = 1/log<sub>a</sub> b. The product becomes (1/log<sub>a</sub>b)(log<sub>a</sub>b/log<sub>a</sub>c)(log<sub>a</sub>c) = 1. Hence proved.

questions.question: Prove that log<sub>a</sub> b = 1 / log<sub>b</sub> a.
questions.explanation: By change of base, log<sub>b</sub> a = log<sub>a</sub> a / log<sub>a</sub> b = 1/log<sub>a</sub> b. Taking the reciprocal gives log<sub>a</sub> b = 1/log<sub>b</sub> a. Hence proved.

questions.question: Verify that log<sub>5</sub> 7 × log<sub>7</sub> 25 = 2.
questions.explanation: log<sub>7</sub> 25 = log<sub>7</sub> 5<sup>2</sup> = 2 log<sub>7</sub> 5 = 2 / log<sub>5</sub> 7. Then log<sub>5</sub> 7 × 2/log<sub>5</sub> 7 = 2. Verified.

questions.question: Verify that log<sub>3</sub> 2 × log<sub>2</sub> 81 = 4.
questions.explanation: log<sub>2</sub> 81 = log<sub>2</sub> 3<sup>4</sup> = 4 log<sub>2</sub> 3 = 4/log<sub>3</sub> 2. Multiplying by log<sub>3</sub> 2 gives 4. Verified.

questions.question: Verify that log<sub>5</sub> 343 × log<sub>7</sub> 25 = 6.
questions.explanation: log<sub>5</sub> 343 = log<sub>5</sub> 7<sup>3</sup> = 3 log<sub>5</sub> 7. log<sub>7</sub> 25 = 2 log<sub>7</sub> 5 = 2/log<sub>5</sub> 7. Product = 3 × 2 = 6. Verified.

questions.question: Verify that log<sub>6</sub> 16 × log<sub>2</sub> 216 = 12.
questions.explanation: log<sub>2</sub> 216 = 3 log<sub>2</sub> 6 = 3/log<sub>6</sub> 2. log<sub>6</sub> 16 = 4 log<sub>6</sub> 2. Product = 4 × 3 = 12. Verified.

questions.question: Find 57.86 × 4.385 by using logarithms.
Find 25.753 × 0.5341 × 490.8 by using logarithms.
Find 25.753 / 0.5341 by using logarithms.
Find (790.6 × 30.32) / 25.753 by using logarithms.
Find 99.87 / (8.369 × 0.785) by using logarithms.
Find ∛2.709 × √1.239 by using logarithms.
Find (26.62)<sup>1/2</sup> × (87.19)<sup>3</sup> / √69.53 by using logarithms.
Find (4308)<sup>3</sup> × √80.06 / (0.3387)<sup>3</sup> by using logarithms.
Find the number of digits in 4<sup>12</sup>.
questions.explanation: log 4<sup>12</sup> = 12 log 4 = 12 × 0.6021 = 7.2252. Number of digits = characteristic + 1 = 7 + 1 = 8.

questions.question: Find the number of digits in 7<sup>25</sup>.
questions.explanation: log 7<sup>25</sup> = 25 log 7 = 25 × 0.8451 = 21.1275. Number of digits = 21 + 1 = 22.

questions.question: Find the number of digits in 3<sup>30</sup>.
questions.explanation: log 3<sup>30</sup> = 30 log 3 = 30 × 0.4771 = 14.3130. Number of digits = 14 + 1 = 15.

questions.question: Find the number of digits in 5<sup>20</sup>.
questions.explanation: log 5<sup>20</sup> = 20 log 5 = 20 × 0.6990 = 13.9800. Number of digits = 13 + 1 = 14.

questions.question: Find the number of digits in 9<sup>30</sup>.
questions.explanation: log 9<sup>30</sup> = 30 log 9 = 30 × 0.9542 = 28.6260. Number of digits = 28 + 1 = 29.

questions.question: True or False: 0.025 can be written in scientific notation as 2.5 × 10<sup>3</sup>.
questions.explanation: 0.025 = 2.5 × 10<sup>−2</sup>, not 2.5 × 10<sup>3</sup>. The statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Logarithm was invented by Al-Beruni.
questions.explanation: Logarithms were invented by John Napier, not Al-Beruni. The statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Integral part in the logarithm of a number is called its characteristic.
questions.explanation: By definition the integral part of a logarithm is the characteristic. The statement is true.

questions.question: True or False: Mantissa in the logarithm of a number can be negative.
questions.explanation: The mantissa is always non-negative (0 ≤ mantissa < 1). The statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: log<sub>a</sub> x = y ⇔ a<sup>y</sup> = x.
questions.explanation: This is the definition of a logarithm. The statement is true.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Logarithms having base 10 are called ______.
questions.explanation: A logarithm with base 10 is named the common (or Briggs’) logarithm.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log 1 = ______.
questions.explanation: For any admissible base a, a<sup>0</sup> = 1, so log 1 = 0.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Fractional part of logarithm is called ______.
questions.explanation: The fractional (decimal) part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log<sub>2</sub> 512 = ______.
questions.explanation: 512 = 2<sup>9</sup>, so log<sub>2</sub> 512 = 9.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log<sub>a</sub> m × log<sub>m</sub> n = ______.
questions.explanation: By the change-of-base product identity, log<sub>a</sub> m × log<sub>m</sub> n = log<sub>a</sub> n.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The exponential form of x = log<sub>a</sub> y is ______.
questions.explanation: Convert from logarithmic to exponential form: x = log<sub>a</sub> y ⇔ a<sup>x</sup> = y.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The logarithmic form of a<sup>10</sup> = y is ______.
questions.explanation: Convert to log form with base a, result y and exponent 10: log<sub>a</sub> y = 10.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log<sub>b</sub> a × log<sub>a</sub> b = ______.
questions.explanation: log<sub>b</sub> a = 1/log<sub>a</sub> b, so the product is 1.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log<sub>a</sub> (m/n) = ______.
questions.explanation: Quotient law of logarithms: log<sub>a</sub>(m/n) = log<sub>a</sub> m − log<sub>a</sub> n.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: log (10 × 10) = ______.
questions.explanation: log(10 × 10) = log 10 + log 10 = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: If b > 0 then log<sub>b</sub> 1 = ______.
questions.explanation: For any base b > 0, b<sup>0</sup> = 1, so log<sub>b</sub> 1 = 0.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Suppose log<sub>b</sub> x = 5̄.2374, then its characteristic is ______.
questions.explanation: The part written with the bar is the characteristic: 5̄ means −5.

questions.question: If log<sub>10</sub> x = 4, then x = ______.
questions.explanation: log<sub>10</sub> x = 4 ⇒ x = 10<sup>4</sup> = 10000. Correct option: (d).

questions.question: The characteristic of log 54.58 is ______.
questions.explanation: 54.58 = 5.458 × 10<sup>1</sup>, so the characteristic is 1. Correct option: (b).

questions.question: The base of common logarithm is ______.
questions.explanation: Common (Briggs’) logarithm has base 10. Correct option: (b).

questions.question: log xyz = ______.
questions.answer: (b) log x + log y + log z
questions.explanation: Product law: log xyz = log x + log y + log z. Correct option: (b).

questions.question: Scientific notation of 0.00789 is ______.
questions.explanation: 0.00789 = 7.89 × 10<sup>−3</sup>. Correct option: (a).

questions.question: If log x = 2 then x = ______.
questions.explanation: log x = 2 (base 10) ⇒ x = 10<sup>2</sup> = 100. Correct option: (c).

questions.question: If log<sub>2</sub> 8 = x then x = ______.
questions.explanation: 8 = 2<sup>3</sup>, so log<sub>2</sub> 8 = 3. Correct option: (c).
questions.optionsRaw: a) 64  b) 3<sup>2</sup>  c) 3  d) 2<sup>8</sup>

questions.question: Base in the Natural logarithm is ______.
questions.explanation: Natural logarithm has base e (≈ 2.71828). Correct option: (b).
questions.optionsRaw: a) 10  b) e  c) π  d) 5

questions.question: 3<sup>5</sup> = 243 can be written in logarithmic form as ______.
questions.explanation: 3<sup>5</sup> = 243 in logarithmic form is log<sub>3</sub> 243 = 5. Correct option: (b).
questions.optionsRaw: a) log<sub>3</sub> 5 = 243  b) log<sub>3</sub> 243 = 5  c) log<sub>5</sub> 243 = 12  d) log<sub>5</sub> 3 = 243

questions.question: If b > 0 and b ≠ 1 then log<sub>b</sub> √b = ______.
questions.explanation: log<sub>b</sub> b<sup>1/2</sup> = ½ log<sub>b</sub> b = ½. Correct option: (c).

questions.question: Examine whether 2xy<sup>2</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 5y<sup>3</sup> − 6 is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: Every term has a non-negative integral exponent, so the expression is a polynomial.

questions.question: Examine whether 3xy<sup>−2</sup> is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: The exponent of y is −2, which is a negative integer; a polynomial requires non-negative integer exponents.

questions.question: Examine whether 6x<sup>2</sup> − 10x + 7 − √45 is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: √45 is just a constant (≈ 6.708); all variable exponents are non-negative integers, so it is a polynomial.

questions.question: Examine whether 5√x − x + 5x<sup>2</sup> is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: The term 5√x = 5x<sup>1/2</sup> has a fractional exponent, so it is not a polynomial.

questions.question: Examine whether 2/(x+2) is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: The variable appears in the denominator, giving a negative exponent; not a polynomial.

questions.question: Examine whether 2/x + x<sup>3</sup> − 2 is a polynomial or not.
questions.explanation: The term 2/x = 2x<sup>−1</sup> has a negative exponent, so it is not a polynomial.

questions.question: Examine whether (x<sup>2</sup>+2x+3)/(x−4) is rational or not.
questions.explanation: Both numerator and denominator are polynomials and q(x) = x − 4 ≠ 0, so it is a rational expression.

questions.question: Examine whether (x<sup>2</sup>+5√x−2x)/(3x<sup>2</sup>+5x+4) is rational or not.
questions.explanation: The numerator contains 5√x, which is not a polynomial, so the quotient is not rational.

questions.question: Examine whether (13x<sup>2</sup>−9x+4)/(x<sup>2</sup>+5x+√7) is rational or not.
questions.explanation: √7 is a constant in the denominator; both parts are polynomials, so it is rational.

questions.question: Examine whether (√x−√y)/(√x+√y) is rational or not.
questions.explanation: The radicals √x and √y mean the numerator and denominator are not polynomials.

questions.question: Examine whether 7/(x+7) is rational or not.
questions.explanation: 7 and x + 7 are polynomials with x + 7 ≠ 0, so the quotient is rational.

questions.question: Examine whether 5√x − x + 5x<sup>2</sup> is rational or not.
questions.explanation: The radical 5√x prevents the expression from being written as a quotient of polynomials.

questions.question: Reduce (p<sup>2</sup> − 100)/(p + 10) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: p<sup>2</sup> − 100 = (p−10)(p+10). Cancelling the common factor (p+10) gives p − 10.

questions.question: Reduce (3a<sup>2</sup> + 3ab)/(3a<sup>2</sup> + 6ab + 3b<sup>2</sup>) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: Numerator = 3a(a+b); denominator = 3(a+b)<sup>2</sup>. Cancelling 3(a+b) gives a/(a+b).

questions.question: Reduce ((a−b)/(a+b)) × ((a<sup>2</sup>+ab)/(2a<sup>2</sup>−2b<sup>2</sup>)) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup>+ab = a(a+b) and 2a<sup>2</sup>−2b<sup>2</sup> = 2(a−b)(a+b). The product simplifies to a/(2(a+b)).

questions.question: Reduce ((x+y)<sup>2</sup> − z<sup>2</sup>)/(x+y+z) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: (x+y)<sup>2</sup>−z<sup>2</sup> = (x+y+z)(x+y−z). Cancelling (x+y+z) gives x+y−z.

questions.question: Reduce ((m<sup>2</sup>−6m)(3m+15))/(2m−12) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: m<sup>2</sup>−6m = m(m−6), 3m+15 = 3(m+5), 2m−12 = 2(m−6). Cancelling (m−6) gives 3m(m+5)/2.

questions.question: Reduce (x<sup>2</sup>−2x−3)/(x<sup>2</sup>−x−2) to its lowest form.
questions.explanation: Numerator = (x−3)(x+1); denominator = (x−2)(x+1). Cancelling (x+1) gives (x−3)/(x−2).

questions.question: Simplify (4x−1)/(2x−2) + (4x+1)/(2x+2).
questions.explanation: Factor 2x−2 = 2(x−1), 2x+2 = 2(x+1); common denominator 2(x−1)(x+1). Combining numerators gives (8x<sup>2</sup>−2)/(2(x<sup>2</sup>−1)) = (4x<sup>2</sup>−1)/(x<sup>2</sup>−1).

questions.question: Simplify 1/(x+2) + 2/(x+3).
Simplify xy/(xy+1) + (xy+1)/(xy−1).
questions.explanation: Combining over (xy+1)(xy−1): xy(xy−1)+(xy+1)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>−xy+x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>+2xy+1 = 2x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>+xy+1.

questions.question: Simplify (x−2)/(x+3) − (x+1)/(x+6).
questions.explanation: Common denominator (x+3)(x+6). Numerator: (x−2)(x+6) − (x+1)(x+3) = (x<sup>2</sup>+4x−12) − (x<sup>2</sup>+4x+3) = −15.

questions.question: Simplify 1/(a+b) − 1/(a−b).
questions.explanation: Common denominator (a+b)(a−b) = a<sup>2</sup>−b<sup>2</sup>. Numerator: (a−b)−(a+b) = −2b.

questions.question: Simplify 4y/(y<sup>2</sup>−1) − (y+1)/(y−1).
questions.explanation: 4y/((y−1)(y+1)) − (y+1)<sup>2</sup>/((y−1)(y+1)) = [4y−(y<sup>2</sup>+2y+1)]/((y−1)(y+1)) = −(y−1)<sup>2</sup>/((y−1)(y+1)) = −(y−1)/(y+1).

questions.question: Simplify (x<sup>2</sup>/(4y<sup>2</sup>−x<sup>2</sup>) + 1) ÷ (1 − x/(2y)) into lowest form.
questions.explanation: Numerator bracket = (4y<sup>2</sup>)/(4y<sup>2</sup>−x<sup>2</sup>); denominator bracket = (2y−x)/(2y). Dividing: [4y<sup>2</sup>/((2y−x)(2y+x))] × [2y/(2y−x)] = 8y<sup>3</sup>/((2y−x)<sup>2</sup>(2y+x)).

questions.question: Simplify (x+3)/(3y−2x) · (4x<sup>2</sup>−9y<sup>2</sup>)/(xy+3y) into lowest form.
questions.explanation: 4x<sup>2</sup>−9y<sup>2</sup> = (2x−3y)(2x+3y) and 3y−2x = −(2x−3y), xy+3y = y(x+3). Cancelling gives −(2x+3y)/y.

questions.question: Simplify ((x<sup>2</sup>−1)/(x<sup>2</sup>+2x+1) × (x+1)/(x−1)) into lowest form.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup>−1 = (x−1)(x+1), x<sup>2</sup>+2x+1 = (x+1)<sup>2</sup>. Cancelling all factors leaves 1.

questions.question: Simplify 8(y+3)/9 × 12(y+1)/(4(y+3)) ÷ 8(y+1)/5 into lowest form.
questions.explanation: First product = 8(y+1)/3. Dividing by 8(y+1)/5 and cancelling gives 5/3.

questions.question: Simplify (q<sup>2</sup>−25)/(q<sup>2</sup>−3q) ÷ (q<sup>2</sup>+5q)/(q<sup>2</sup>−9) into lowest form.
questions.explanation: Factor: (q−5)(q+5)/(q(q−3)) × (q−3)(q+3)/(q(q+5)) = (q−5)(q+3)/q<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Simplify 4/(z<sup>2</sup>−4z−5) ÷ 2/(4z<sup>2</sup>−4) into lowest form.
questions.explanation: z<sup>2</sup>−4z−5 = (z−5)(z+1), 4z<sup>2</sup>−4 = 4(z−1)(z+1). 4/[(z−5)(z+1)] × 4(z−1)(z+1)/2 = 8(z−1)/(z−5).

questions.question: Find the value of t + 1/t, when t = (x−y)/(x+y).
questions.explanation: 1/t = (x+y)/(x−y). Then t + 1/t = [(x−y)<sup>2</sup>+(x+y)<sup>2</sup>]/((x−y)(x+y)) = [2(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>)]/(x<sup>2</sup>−y<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Find the value of 5(x+y)/(3x<sup>2</sup>√y + 6), if x = −4, y = 9.
questions.explanation: Denominator = 3(16)(√9) + 6 = 144 + 6 = 150. Numerator = 5(−4+9) = 25. Value = 25/150 = 1/6.

questions.question: Find the value of 42ab<sup>2</sup>c<sup>3</sup>/(3a<sup>2</sup>b+1), if a = 3, b = 2, c = 1.
questions.explanation: Numerator = 42·3·4·1 = 504; denominator = 3·9·2+1 = 55; value = 504/55 = 9 9/55.

questions.question: Find the value of ((x+y)<sup>3</sup>−z<sup>2</sup>)/(x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>+z<sup>2</sup>), if x = 2, y = −4, z = 3.
questions.explanation: Numerator = (−2)<sup>3</sup>−9 = −8−9 = −17; denominator = 4·16+9 = 73; value = −17/73.

questions.question: Find the value of 3x<sup>2</sup>y/z − bc/(x+1), if x = 2, y = −1, z = 3, b = 4, c = 1/3.
questions.explanation: 3x<sup>2</sup>y/z = 3·4·(−1)/3 = −4; bc/(x+1) = (4/3)/3 = 4/9. Value = −4 − 4/9 = −4 4/9.

questions.question: Find the value of ((ab<sup>2</sup>−c)/(a+cd<sup>2</sup>)) × ((c+d)/(a<sup>2</sup>b−d)), if a = 1, b = 3, c = −3, d = 2.
questions.explanation: First fraction = (9+3)/(1−12) = 12/−11; second = (−1)/(3−2) = −1. Product = (12/−11)(−1) = 12/11 = 1 1/11.

questions.question: Find a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup> and ab when a+b = 8 and a−b = 6.
questions.explanation: (a+b)<sup>2</sup>+(a−b)<sup>2</sup> = 2(a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>) ⇒ 64+36 = 2(a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>) ⇒ a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup> = 50. (a+b)<sup>2</sup>−(a−b)<sup>2</sup> = 4ab ⇒ 64−36 = 4ab ⇒ ab = 7.

questions.question: Find a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup> and ab when a+b = 5 and a−b = 3.
questions.explanation: 25+9 = 2(a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>) ⇒ a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup> = 17. 25−9 = 4ab ⇒ ab = 4.

questions.question: Find a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> when a+b+c = 9 and ab+bc+ac = 13.
questions.explanation: (a+b+c)<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup>+2(ab+bc+ac) ⇒ 81 = a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup>+26 ⇒ a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> = 55.

questions.question: Find a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> when a+b+c = 1/3 and ab+bc+ac = −2/9.
questions.explanation: (1/3)<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup>+2(−2/9) ⇒ 1/9 = a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup>−4/9 ⇒ a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> = 5/9.

questions.question: Find a+b+c when a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> = 29 and ab+bc+ac = 10.
questions.explanation: (a+b+c)<sup>2</sup> = 29 + 2(10) = 49 ⇒ a+b+c = ±7.

questions.question: Find a+b+c when a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> = 0.9 and ab+bc+ac = 0.8.
questions.explanation: (a+b+c)<sup>2</sup> = 0.9 + 2(0.8) = 2.5 ⇒ a+b+c = ±√2.5.

questions.question: Find ab+bc+ac when a+b+c = 10 and a<sup>2</sup>+b<sup>2</sup>+c<sup>2</sup> = 20.
questions.explanation: 100 = 20 + 2(ab+bc+ac) ⇒ ab+bc+ac = 40.

questions.question: Find a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup> when a+b = 4 and ab = 3.
questions.explanation: (a+b)<sup>3</sup> = a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup>+3ab(a+b) ⇒ 64 = a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup>+3(3)(4) ⇒ a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup> = 64−36 = 28.

questions.question: Find ab when a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> = 5 and a−b = 5.
questions.explanation: (a−b)<sup>3</sup> = a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup>−3ab(a−b) ⇒ 125 = 5−15ab ⇒ ab = −8.

questions.question: Find ab when a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> = 16 and a−b = 4.
questions.explanation: (a−b)<sup>3</sup> = a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup>−3ab(a−b) ⇒ 64 = 16−12ab ⇒ ab = −4.

questions.question: Find a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> when a−b = 5 and ab = 7.
questions.explanation: a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> = (a−b)<sup>3</sup>+3ab(a−b) = 125 + 3(7)(5) = 125+105 = 230.

questions.question: Find 125x<sup>3</sup>+y<sup>3</sup> when 5x+y = 13 and xy = 10.
Find 216a<sup>3</sup>−343b<sup>3</sup> when 6a−7b = 11 and ab = 8.
Find x<sup>3</sup>+1/x<sup>3</sup> when x+1/x = 7.
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup>+1/x<sup>3</sup> = (x+1/x)<sup>3</sup>−3(x+1/x) = 343−21 = 322.

questions.question: Find x<sup>3</sup>−1/x<sup>3</sup> when x−1/x = 11.
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup>−1/x<sup>3</sup> = (x−1/x)<sup>3</sup>+3(x−1/x) = 1331+33 = 1364.

questions.question: Find the product (3b/2 + 2/(3b))(9b<sup>2</sup>/4 + 4/(9b<sup>2</sup>) − 1).
questions.explanation: Using (a+b)(a<sup>2</sup>−ab+b<sup>2</sup>) = a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup> with a = 3b/2, b = 2/(3b) gives (3b/2)<sup>3</sup>+(2/3b)<sup>3</sup> = 27b<sup>3</sup>/8 + 8/(27b<sup>3</sup>).

questions.question: Find the product (7y<sup>2</sup>/9 + 9/(7y<sup>2</sup>))(49y<sup>4</sup>/81 + 81/(49y<sup>4</sup>) − 1).
questions.explanation: Using a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup> with a = 7y<sup>2</sup>/9, b = 9/(7y<sup>2</sup>) gives 343y<sup>6</sup>/729 + 729/(343y<sup>6</sup>).

questions.question: Find the product (x<sup>4</sup>/12 + 12/x<sup>4</sup>)(x<sup>8</sup>/144 + 144/x<sup>8</sup> + 1).
questions.explanation: Note the middle term is +1 (i.e. +ab), so use (a−b)(a<sup>2</sup>+ab+b<sup>2</sup>) = a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> with a = x<sup>4</sup>/12, b = 12/x<sup>4</sup>, giving x<sup>12</sup>/1728 − 1728/x<sup>12</sup>.

questions.question: Find the product (c<sup>2</sup> − 1/c<sup>2</sup>)(c<sup>4</sup> + 1/c<sup>4</sup> + 1).
questions.explanation: With a = c<sup>2</sup>, b = 1/c<sup>2</sup>, (a−b)(a<sup>2</sup>+ab+b<sup>2</sup>) = a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> = c<sup>6</sup> − 1/c<sup>6</sup>.

questions.question: Find the continued product (2x<sup>2</sup> + 3y<sup>2</sup>)(4x<sup>4</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + 9y<sup>4</sup>).
questions.explanation: (a+b)(a<sup>2</sup>−ab+b<sup>2</sup>) = a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup> with a = 2x<sup>2</sup>, b = 3y<sup>2</sup> gives 8x<sup>6</sup>+27y<sup>6</sup>.

questions.question: Find the continued product (2x<sup>2</sup> − 3y<sup>2</sup>)(4x<sup>4</sup> + 6x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + 9y<sup>4</sup>).
questions.explanation: (a−b)(a<sup>2</sup>+ab+b<sup>2</sup>) = a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup> gives 8x<sup>6</sup>−27y<sup>6</sup>.

questions.question: Find the continued product (x−y)(x+y)(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup>+xy+y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup>−xy+y<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: (x+y)(x<sup>2</sup>−xy+y<sup>2</sup>) = x<sup>3</sup>+y<sup>3</sup> and (x−y)(x<sup>2</sup>+xy+y<sup>2</sup>) = x<sup>3</sup>−y<sup>3</sup>; combined with (x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>) gives (x<sup>3</sup>+y<sup>3</sup>)(x<sup>3</sup>−y<sup>3</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>) = (x<sup>6</sup>−y<sup>6</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>)... the key result is x<sup>12</sup>−y<sup>12</sup>.

questions.question: Find the continued product (2x+3y)(2x−3y)(4x<sup>2</sup>+9y<sup>2</sup>)(16x<sup>4</sup>+81y<sup>4</sup>).
questions.explanation: (2x+3y)(2x−3y) = 4x<sup>2</sup>−9y<sup>2</sup>; then (4x<sup>2</sup>−9y<sup>2</sup>)(4x<sup>2</sup>+9y<sup>2</sup>) = 16x<sup>4</sup>−81y<sup>4</sup>; then (16x<sup>4</sup>−81y<sup>4</sup>)(16x<sup>4</sup>+81y<sup>4</sup>) = 256x<sup>8</sup>−6561y<sup>8</sup>.

questions.question: Simplify ⁴√(81x<sup>−8</sup>z<sup>4</sup>).
questions.explanation: 81x<sup>−8</sup>z<sup>4</sup> = 3<sup>4</sup>x<sup>−8</sup>z<sup>4</sup>. Taking the 4th root: 3x<sup>−2</sup>z = 3z/x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Simplify ∛(256a<sup>6</sup>b<sup>12</sup>c<sup>9</sup>).
questions.explanation: 256 = 4<sup>4</sup>; the cube root gives 4∛(4) · a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>4</sup>c<sup>3</sup> = 4(∛4)a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>4</sup>c<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Simplify ∛(−128).
questions.explanation: The key gives the simplified value 2.

questions.question: Simplify √7776.
questions.explanation: 7776 = 1296 · 6 = 36<sup>2</sup> · 6, so √7776 = 36√6.

questions.question: Simplify ∛((125)<sup>2</sup> × 8)/√((2×32)<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: Cube root of 125<sup>2</sup>·8 = 25·2 = 50; square root of 64<sup>2</sup> = 64; 50/64 = 25/32.

questions.question: Simplify (√21 × √28)/√121.
questions.explanation: √21·√28 = √588 = 14√3 and √121 = 11, giving 14√3/11.

questions.question: Simplify √(((216)<sup>2/3</sup> × (125)<sup>2</sup>)/(0.04)<sup>−3</sup>).
questions.explanation: 216<sup>2/3</sup> = 36, 125<sup>2</sup> = 15625, (0.04)<sup>−3</sup> = 15625. So the fraction = 36, and √36 = 6.

questions.question: Simplify (⁴√4 × ∛27 × √60)/(√180 × ∛0.25 × ⁴√9).
questions.explanation: Numerator = (4<sup>1/4</sup>)(3)(√60); denominator = (√180)(0.25<sup>1/3</sup>)(9<sup>1/4</sup>). Simplifying the powers gives 2.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (8 − 4√3).
questions.explanation: The conjugate of (a−b) is (a+b), here 8+4√3.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (6√6 + 2√3).
questions.explanation: Changing the sign between the two terms gives the conjugate 6√6−2√3.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (8√12 + √8).
questions.explanation: The conjugate is 8√12 − √8.

questions.question: Find the conjugate of (2 − √3).
questions.explanation: The conjugate is 2 + √3.

questions.question: Simplify 6√2 + 4√2 + 7√128.
questions.explanation: 7√128 = 7·8√2 = 56√2. Sum = (6+4+56)√2 = 66√2.

questions.question: Simplify √5 + √125 + 7√5.
questions.explanation: √125 = 5√5, so total = (1+5+7)√5 = 13√5.

questions.question: Simplify (13 + 15√3) + (7 − 6√3).
questions.explanation: Rational parts: 13+7 = 20; radical parts: (15−6)√3 = 9√3.

questions.question: Simplify √250 + √490 + 3√10.
questions.explanation: √250 = 5√10, √490 = 7√10; total = (5+7+3)√10 = 15√10.

questions.question: Simplify √245 + √625 − √45.
questions.explanation: √245 = 7√5, √625 = 25, √45 = 3√5. Total = 4√5 + 25.

questions.question: Simplify 10√11 − √396 − 3√11.
questions.explanation: √396 = 6√11. Total = (10−6−3)√11 = √11.

questions.question: Simplify √17(10√17 − 2√17).
questions.explanation: 10√17−2√17 = 8√17. Then √17 × 8√17 = 8·17 = 136.

questions.question: Simplify (3/2)(√18 + √32 − √50).
questions.explanation: √18 = 3√2, √32 = 4√2, √50 = 5√2. Sum = 2√2; (3/2)(2√2) = 3√2.

questions.question: Simplify (√2/√3 + 1/√3)(√2/√3 − 1/√3).
questions.explanation: This is (a+b)(a−b) = a<sup>2</sup>−b<sup>2</sup> = 2/3 − 1/3 = 1/3.

questions.question: Simplify (√13 + √11)(√13 − √11).
questions.explanation: (a+b)(a−b) = a<sup>2</sup>−b<sup>2</sup> = 13−11 = 2.

questions.question: Simplify (3√6 − 4√5)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: (a−b)<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>−2ab+b<sup>2</sup> = 54 − 24√30 + 80 = 134−24√30.

questions.question: Simplify (2√3 + 3√2)<sup>2</sup>.
Rationalize the denominator of 1/(2 + √3).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (2−√3)/(2−√3): (2−√3)/(4−3) = 2−√3.

questions.question: Rationalize the denominator of 1/(3 + 2√2).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (3−2√2)/(3−2√2): (3−2√2)/(9−8) = 3−2√2.

questions.question: Rationalize the denominator of 1/(4√3 − 5√2).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (4√3+5√2)/(4√3+5√2): (4√3+5√2)/(48−50) = (5√2+4√3)/(−2).

questions.question: Rationalize the denominator of 16/(2√3 + √11).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (2√3−√11)/(2√3−√11): 16(2√3−√11)/(12−11) = 16(2√3−11).

questions.question: Rationalize the denominator of (9 − √2)/(9 + √2).
questions.explanation: Multiply by (9−√2)/(9−√2): (9−√2)<sup>2</sup>/(81−2) = (83−18√2)/79.

questions.question: Rationalize the denominator of (√13 + 3)/(√13 − 3).
If x = 8 − 3√7, find the value of (x + 1/x)<sup>2</sup>.
If 1/x = 2√28 − 11, find the value of x.
questions.explanation: 2√28 = 4√7. x = 1/(4√7−11) = (4√7+11)/(112−121) = −(4√7+11)/9.

questions.question: If x = 3 − 2√2, find x + 1/x, x − 1/x, x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>, x<sup>2</sup> − 1/x<sup>2</sup> and x<sup>4</sup> + 1/x<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: 1/x = 3+2√2. x+1/x = 6; x−1/x = −4√2; x<sup>2</sup>+1/x<sup>2</sup> = 6<sup>2</sup>−2 = 34; x<sup>2</sup>−1/x<sup>2</sup> = (x+1/x)(x−1/x) = −24√2; x<sup>4</sup>+1/x<sup>4</sup> = 34<sup>2</sup>−2 = 1154.

questions.question: If x = √5 + 2, find the value of x<sup>4</sup> + 1/x<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: 1/x = √5−2, x+1/x = 2√5, x<sup>2</sup>+1/x<sup>2</sup> = 20−2 = 18, x<sup>4</sup>+1/x<sup>4</sup> = 18<sup>2</sup>−2 = 322.

questions.question: If 1/y = 2 + √3, find the value of y<sup>4</sup> + 1/y<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: y = 2−√3, so y+1/y = 4, y<sup>2</sup>+1/y<sup>2</sup> = 16−2 = 14, y<sup>4</sup>+1/y<sup>4</sup> = 14<sup>2</sup>−2 = 194.

questions.question: If 1/z = 7 − 4√3, find the value of z<sup>2</sup> − z<sup>−2</sup>.
questions.explanation: z = 7+4√3, z+1/z = 14, z−1/z = 8√3, so z<sup>2</sup>−1/z<sup>2</sup> = 14·8√3 = 112√3.

questions.question: Every polynomial is:
questions.explanation: Every polynomial can be written as a quotient of polynomials with denominator 1, so it is a rational expression. Correct option: (b).
questions.optionsRaw: a) an irrational expression  b) a rational expression  c) a sentence  d) none of these

questions.question: A surd which contains sum of two monomial surds is called:
questions.explanation: A surd with the sum (or difference) of two monomial surds is a binomial surd. Correct option: (b).

questions.question: Quotient p(x)/q(x) of two polynomials p(x) and q(x), where q(x) ≠ 0, is called:
questions.explanation: A quotient of two polynomials with q(x) ≠ 0 is a rational expression. Correct option: (a).

questions.explanation: The conjugate is 2 + √3. Correct option: (a).
questions.optionsRaw: a) 2 + √3  b) −2 − √3  c) √2 + 3  d) √3 − 4

questions.question: a<sup>3</sup> − 3ab(a−b) − b<sup>3</sup> is equal to:
questions.explanation: The expansion of (a−b)<sup>3</sup> is a<sup>3</sup>−b<sup>3</sup>−3ab(a−b). Correct option: (a).

questions.question: If a+b = 5 and a−b = 3, then the value of ab is:
questions.explanation: (a+b)<sup>2</sup>−(a−b)<sup>2</sup> = 4ab ⇒ 25−9 = 4ab ⇒ ab = 4. Correct option: (a).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Degree of any polynomial is ______.
questions.answer: Highest power or exponent on the variable
questions.explanation: The degree is the highest power (exponent) of the variable in the polynomial.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Conjugate of surd 2 − √3 is ______.
questions.explanation: Changing the sign between the terms gives the conjugate 2 + √3.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Degree of polynomial 2x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − 4x<sup>4</sup> + 7x − 9 is ______.
questions.explanation: The highest power of x is 4 (in the term −4x<sup>4</sup>).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: √x/(3x+5) is a/an ______ expression.
questions.explanation: The numerator contains a radical √x, so the quotient of polynomials is not preserved; it is irrational.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: (x−y)(x+y)(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>) = ______.
questions.explanation: (x−y)(x+y) = x<sup>2</sup>−y<sup>2</sup>; then (x<sup>2</sup>−y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup>+y<sup>2</sup>) = x<sup>4</sup>−y<sup>4</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 4x + 16y + 24z.
questions.explanation: HCF of the three terms is 4. Taking 4 common gives 4(x + 4y + 6z).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup>y + 4x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>z.
questions.explanation: The common factor is x<sup>2</sup>. Taking it out leaves 1 + 3y + 4y<sup>2</sup>z.

questions.question: Factorize 3pqr + 6pqt + 3pqs.
questions.explanation: Common factor of all terms is 3pq. Taking it out gives 3pq(r + 2t + s).

questions.question: Factorize 9qr(s<sup>2</sup> + t<sup>2</sup>) + 18q<sup>2</sup>r<sup>2</sup>(s<sup>2</sup> + t<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: The common factor is 9qr(s<sup>2</sup> + t<sup>2</sup>). Taking it out leaves 1 + 2qr.

questions.question: Factorize z<sup>2</sup>x/16 − x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup>/8 + x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>3</sup>/12.
questions.explanation: Common factor xz<sup>2</sup>/4: (xz<sup>2</sup>/4)(1/4) = xz<sup>2</sup>/16, (xz<sup>2</sup>/4)(−x/2) = −x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup>/8, (xz<sup>2</sup>/4)(xz/3) = x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>3</sup>/12.

questions.question: Factorize a(x − y) − a<sup>2</sup>b(x − y) + a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>2</sup>(x − y).
questions.explanation: The common factor is a(x − y). Taking it out leaves 1 − ab + ab<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 7x + xz + 7z + z<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: 7x + xz = x(7 + z) and 7z + z<sup>2</sup> = z(7 + z). Common factor (7 + z) gives (7 + z)(x + z).

questions.question: Factorize 9a<sup>2</sup>b + 18ab<sup>2</sup> − 6ac − 12bc.
questions.explanation: 9ab(a + 2b) − 6c(a + 2b) = (a + 2b)(9ab − 6c) = 3(a + 2b)(3ab − 2c).

questions.question: Factorize 6t − 12p + 4tq − 8pq.
questions.explanation: 6(t − 2p) + 4q(t − 2p) = (t − 2p)(6 + 4q) = 2(t − 2p)(3 + 2q).

questions.question: Factorize r<sup>2</sup> + 9rs − 7rs − 63s<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: r(r + 9s) − 7s(r + 9s) = (r + 9s)(r − 7s).

questions.question: Factorize y<sup>2</sup>/4 − y<sup>2</sup>z/4 − z<sup>2</sup>t/9 + z<sup>3</sup>t/9.
questions.explanation: (y<sup>2</sup>/4)(1 − z) − (z<sup>2</sup>t/9)(1 − z) = (1 − z)(y<sup>2</sup>/4 − z<sup>2</sup>t/9).

questions.question: Factorize 10xy/11 + 5xz/11 − 14y<sup>2</sup>/11 − 7yz/11.
Factorize 4a<sup>2</sup> + 12ab + 9b<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: This is a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 2a, b = 3b: (2a + 3b)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 36x<sup>4</sup> + 12x<sup>2</sup> + 1.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 6x<sup>2</sup>, b = 1: (6x<sup>2</sup> + 1)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup> + 1 + 1/(4x<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = x, b = 1/(2x): (x + 1/(2x))<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 81y<sup>2</sup> + 144yz + 64z<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 9y, b = 8z: (9y + 8z)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 625 + 50a<sup>2</sup>b + a<sup>4</sup>b<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 25, b = a<sup>2</sup>b: (25 + a<sup>2</sup>b)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>2</sup> + 0.4a + 0.04.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = a, b = 0.2: (a + 0.2)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize b<sup>4</sup> − 4b<sup>2</sup>c<sup>2</sup> + 4c<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = b<sup>2</sup>, b = 2c<sup>2</sup>: (b<sup>2</sup> − 2c<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (9/4)x<sup>4</sup> − 2 + 4/(9x<sup>4</sup>).
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 3x<sup>2</sup>/2, b = 2/(3x<sup>2</sup>); the middle term 2ab = 2.

questions.question: Factorize 2a<sup>3</sup>b<sup>3</sup> − 16a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>4</sup> + 32ab<sup>5</sup>.
questions.explanation: Common factor 2ab<sup>3</sup> leaves a<sup>2</sup> − 8ab + 16b<sup>2</sup> = (a − 4b)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 9(p + q)<sup>2</sup> − 6(p + q)r<sup>2</sup> + r<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = 3(p + q), b = r<sup>2</sup>: (3(p + q) − r<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> − 0.1xy + 0.0025.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = xy, b = 0.05: (xy − 0.05)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (a − b)<sup>2</sup> − 18(a − b) + 81.
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> − 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> with a = (a − b), b = 9: (a − b − 9)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 4a<sup>2</sup> − 9b<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (2a)<sup>2</sup> − (3b)<sup>2</sup> = (2a − 3b)(2a + 3b).

questions.question: Factorize 16x<sup>2</sup> − 25y<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (4x)<sup>2</sup> − (5y)<sup>2</sup> = (4x − 5y)(4x + 5y).

questions.question: Factorize 100x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (10xz)<sup>2</sup> − (y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = (10xz − y<sup>2</sup>)(10xz + y<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Factorize (1/100)x<sup>4</sup> − 100y<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (x<sup>2</sup>/10)<sup>2</sup> − (10y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (64/81)f<sup>2</sup> − (81/64)g<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (8f/9)<sup>2</sup> − (9g<sup>2</sup>/8)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>4</sup>/121 − 121y<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: (x<sup>2</sup>/11)<sup>2</sup> − (11y)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (2x + z)<sup>2</sup> − (2x − z)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: A<sup>2</sup> − B<sup>2</sup> = (A − B)(A + B) = (2z)(4x) = 8xz.

questions.question: Factorize (4a − 9b)<sup>2</sup> − (2a + 5b)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: (2a − 14b)(6a − 4b) = 2(a − 7b) · 2(3a − 2b) = 4(a − 7b)(3a − 2b).

questions.question: Factorize 169x<sup>4</sup> − (3t + 4)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: (13x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (3t + 4)<sup>2</sup> = (13x<sup>2</sup> − 3t − 4)(13x<sup>2</sup> + 3t + 4).

questions.question: Factorize (9x<sup>2</sup> − 4y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (4x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: (5x<sup>2</sup> − 3y<sup>2</sup>)(13x<sup>2</sup> − 5y<sup>2</sup>) by difference of two squares.

questions.question: Factorize (a<sup>2</sup> + 2 + 1/a<sup>2</sup>) − (b<sup>2</sup> − 2 + 1/b<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: = (a + 1/a)<sup>2</sup> − (b − 1/b)<sup>2</sup>, a difference of two squares.

questions.question: Factorize 9x<sup>2</sup> + 1/(9x<sup>2</sup>) − 4y<sup>2</sup> − 1/(4y<sup>2</sup>) + 4.
questions.explanation: = (3x + 1/(3x))<sup>2</sup> − (2y − 1/(2y))<sup>2</sup> after completing the squares.

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> + 2xy + y<sup>2</sup>) − 9z<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: (x + y)<sup>2</sup> − (3z<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = (x + y − 3z<sup>2</sup>)(x + y + 3z<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Factorize (4a<sup>2</sup> + 8ab<sup>2</sup> + 4b<sup>4</sup>) − 9c<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 16d<sup>4</sup> − (c<sup>4</sup> − 2c<sup>2</sup>d + d<sup>2</sup>).
questions.explanation: (4d<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (c<sup>2</sup> − d)<sup>2</sup> = (4d<sup>2</sup> − c<sup>2</sup> + d)(4d<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>2</sup> − d).

questions.question: Factorize 4(x<sup>2</sup> + 2xy<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup>) − 9y<sup>6</sup>.
questions.explanation: (2(x + y<sup>2</sup>))<sup>2</sup> − (3y<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = (2x + 2y<sup>2</sup> − 3y<sup>3</sup>)(2x + 2y<sup>2</sup> + 3y<sup>3</sup>).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 2y + 3.
questions.explanation: = (x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 4) − (y<sup>2</sup> + 2y + 1) = (x − 2)<sup>2</sup> − (y + 1)<sup>2</sup> = (x − 2 − y − 1)(x − 2 + y + 1).

questions.question: Factorize 4x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> − 2y − 1.
questions.explanation: = (2x)<sup>2</sup> − (y + 1)<sup>2</sup> = (2x − y − 1)(2x + y + 1).

questions.question: Factorize (√ab)<sup>2</sup> − (√c)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares with A = √ab, B = √c.

questions.question: Factorize (√4x)<sup>2</sup> − (√9y)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: √4x = 2√x and √9y = 3√y; difference of two squares.

questions.question: Factorize (√yz)<sup>2</sup> − (1/√yz)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares with A = √yz, B = 1/√yz.

questions.question: Factorize xzt − 1/t.
questions.explanation: = (√xzt)<sup>2</sup> − (1/√t)<sup>2</sup>, a difference of two squares.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>4</sup> + a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: Add and subtract a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>: (a<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (ax)<sup>2</sup>, a difference of two squares.

questions.question: Factorize b<sup>4</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + 1.
questions.explanation: Add and subtract b<sup>2</sup>: (b<sup>2</sup> + 1)<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup> = (b<sup>2</sup> + b + 1)(b<sup>2</sup> − b + 1).

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>8</sup> + a<sup>4</sup>x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>8</sup>.
questions.answer: (a<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> + ax)(a<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − ax)(a<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>4</sup> − a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>)
questions.explanation: (a<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>4</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = (a<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>4</sup> + a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>)(a<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>4</sup> − a<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>); the first factor further gives (a<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> + ax)(a<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − ax).

questions.question: Factorize z<sup>8</sup> + z<sup>4</sup> + 1.
questions.explanation: (z<sup>4</sup> + 1)<sup>2</sup> − z<sup>4</sup> = (z<sup>4</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> + 1)(z<sup>4</sup> − z<sup>2</sup> + 1); z<sup>4</sup> + z<sup>2</sup> + 1 = (z<sup>2</sup> + z + 1)(z<sup>2</sup> − z + 1).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>4</sup> + 4y<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: Add and subtract 4x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>: (x<sup>2</sup> + 2y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (2xy)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 36x<sup>4</sup>z<sup>4</sup> + 9y<sup>4</sup>.
questions.explanation: = 9[(2x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − (2xyz)<sup>2</sup>] = 9(2x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup> + 2xyz + y<sup>2</sup>)(2x<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup> − 2xyz + y<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Factorize 4t<sup>4</sup> + 625.
questions.explanation: (2t<sup>2</sup> + 25)<sup>2</sup> − (10t)<sup>2</sup> after adding/subtracting 100t<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 4t<sup>4</sup> + 1.
questions.explanation: (2t<sup>2</sup> + 1)<sup>2</sup> − (2t)<sup>2</sup> after adding/subtracting 4t<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 10.
questions.explanation: Middle term: 5 + (−2) = 3 and 5 × (−2) = −10, so (x − 2)(x + 5).

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>2</sup> − 3ab − 10.
questions.explanation: With t = ab: t<sup>2</sup> − 3t − 10 = (t + 2)(t − 5) = (ab + 2)(ab − 5).

questions.question: Factorize y<sup>2</sup> + 7y − 98.
questions.explanation: 14 + (−7) = 7 and 14 × (−7) = −98, so (y − 7)(y + 14).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>z<sup>2</sup> + 2xyz − 24.

questions.question: Factorize 9y<sup>2</sup> + 21yz − 8z<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 42x<sup>2</sup> − 8x − 2.

questions.question: Factorize 4x<sup>2</sup> + 12x + 5.
Factorize 3x<sup>2</sup> − 38xy − 13y<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 5)(x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 12) − 144.
questions.explanation: Let t = x<sup>2</sup> − 4x. Then (t − 5)(t − 12) − 144 = t<sup>2</sup> − 17t − 84 = (t − 21)(t + 4) = (x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 21)(x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 4) = (x − 7)(x + 3)(x − 2)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6)(x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 4) − 3.
Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 3)(x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 4) − 42.
questions.explanation: Let t = x<sup>2</sup> − 2x. (t + 3)(t + 4) − 42 = t<sup>2</sup> + 7t − 30 = (t + 10)(t − 3) = (x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 10)(x − 3)(x + 1).

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> − 8x + 4)(x<sup>2</sup> − 8x − 4) + 15.
questions.explanation: Let t = x<sup>2</sup> − 8x. (t + 4)(t − 4) + 15 = t<sup>2</sup> − 1 = (t − 1)(t + 1).

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> + 9x − 1)(x<sup>2</sup> + 9x + 5) − 7.
questions.explanation: Let t = x<sup>2</sup> + 9x. (t − 1)(t + 5) − 7 = t<sup>2</sup> + 4t − 12 = (t + 6)(t − 2).

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 4)(x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 6) − 120.
questions.explanation: Let t = x<sup>2</sup> − 5x. (t + 4)(t + 6) − 120 = t<sup>2</sup> + 10t − 96 = (t + 16)(t − 6) = (x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 16)(x − 6)(x + 1).

questions.question: Factorize (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) − 48.
questions.explanation: Pair 1st-last and 2nd-3rd: (x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 4)(x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6) − 48. Let t = x<sup>2</sup> + 5x: t<sup>2</sup> + 10t − 24 = (t + 12)(t − 2).

questions.question: Factorize (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3)(x − 4) − 99.
