questions.question: Factorize (x − 3)(x − 5)(x − 7)(x − 9) + 15.

questions.question: Factorize (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3)(x − 4) − 224.

questions.question: Factorize (x − 2)(x − 3)(x + 2)(x + 3) − 2x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (x − 2)(x + 2)(x − 4)(x + 4) − 14x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (x + 5)(x + 2)(x − 5)(x − 2) + 4x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize (x<sup>2</sup> − x − 12)(x<sup>2</sup> − x − 12) − x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize b<sup>3</sup> + 3b<sup>2</sup>c + 3bc<sup>2</sup> + c<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 8x<sup>3</sup> + 12x<sup>2</sup>y + 6xy<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 8x<sup>3</sup> + 36x<sup>2</sup> + 54x + 27.

questions.question: Factorize z<sup>3</sup>/8 + z<sup>2</sup>y/4 + zy<sup>2</sup>/6 + y<sup>3</sup>/27.

questions.question: Factorize d<sup>3</sup> − 6d<sup>2</sup>c + 12dc<sup>2</sup> − 8c<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>6</sup> + (16/3)x<sup>2</sup> − 4x<sup>4</sup> − 64/27.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup>/125 − (3/25)x<sup>2</sup>y + (3/5)xy<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize z<sup>3</sup>/27 − 2z<sup>2</sup>y + 36zy<sup>2</sup> − 216y<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 216 + (9/2)z<sup>2</sup> − 54z − z<sup>3</sup>/8.

questions.question: Factorize (8/27)x<sup>3</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup>y + (9/2)xy<sup>2</sup> − (27/8)y<sup>3</sup>.
questions.explanation: a<sup>3</sup> − 3a<sup>2</sup>b + 3ab<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>3</sup> with a = 2x/3, b = 3y/2.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>11</sup> + a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>9</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>6</sup> + 1.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>3</sup>b<sup>3</sup> + 512.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup>/125 + 125/x<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>9</sup> + x<sup>3</sup>y<sup>6</sup>z<sup>9</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>6</sup>/27 + 8/x<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> − 8y<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 1000 − x<sup>3</sup>y<sup>3</sup>/125.

questions.question: Factorize a<sup>6</sup> − b<sup>6</sup>.

questions.explanation: (a<sup>3</sup> − b<sup>3</sup>)(a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup>), then each cube factors further.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>6</sup>/64 − 64/x<sup>12</sup>.
questions.explanation: Difference of squares (x<sup>3</sup>/8)<sup>2</sup> − (8/x<sup>6</sup>)<sup>2</sup>, then each factor is a difference/sum of cubes.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>12</sup> − y<sup>12</sup>.
questions.answer: (x − y)(x + y)(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>4</sup> − x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>)
questions.explanation: (x<sup>6</sup> − y<sup>6</sup>)(x<sup>6</sup> + y<sup>6</sup>); x<sup>6</sup> − y<sup>6</sup> = (x<sup>3</sup> − y<sup>3</sup>)(x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup>) and x<sup>6</sup> + y<sup>6</sup> = (x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>4</sup> − x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup>).

questions.question: Factorize 27/x<sup>3</sup> − 8y<sup>6</sup>.
questions.explanation: (3/x)<sup>3</sup> − (2y<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup>; a = 3/x, b = 2y<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize 8x<sup>6</sup> − 1/729.
questions.explanation: (2x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3</sup> − (1/9)<sup>3</sup>; a = 2x<sup>2</sup>, b = 1/9.

questions.question: Find the remainder when x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x − 8 is divided by (x − 1).
questions.explanation: By remainder theorem, put x = 1: p(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 8 = −2.

questions.question: Find the remainder when x<sup>3</sup> + 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 8 is divided by (x + 1).
questions.explanation: Put x = −1: p(−1) = −1 + 6 − 11 + 8 = 2.

questions.question: Find the remainder when x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> + 14 is divided by (x − 2).
Find the remainder when x<sup>3</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 14 is divided by (x + 2).
questions.explanation: Put x = −2: p(−2) = −8 − 12 − 8 − 14 = −42.

questions.question: Find the remainder when (2y − 1)<sup>3</sup> + 6(3 + 4y) − 9 is divided by (2y + 1).
questions.explanation: Put 2y + 1 = 0, i.e. y = −1/2: (−2)<sup>3</sup> + 6(3 − 2) − 9 = −8 + 6 − 9 = −11.

questions.question: Find the remainder when 4y<sup>3</sup> − 4y + 3 is divided by (2y − 1).
Find the remainder when (2y + 1)<sup>3</sup> − 6(3 − 4y) − 10 is divided by (2y − 1).
questions.explanation: Put y = 1/2: 2<sup>3</sup> − 6(3 − 2) − 10 = 8 − 6 − 10 = −8.

questions.question: Find the remainder when x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup> is divided by (x − y).
questions.explanation: Put x = y: y<sup>4</sup> + y<sup>4</sup> + y<sup>4</sup> = 3y<sup>4</sup>.

questions.question: Find m if p(y) = my<sup>3</sup> + 4y<sup>2</sup> + 3y − 4 and q(y) = y<sup>3</sup> − 4y + m leave the same remainder when divided by (y − 3).
questions.explanation: p(3) = 27m + 36 + 9 − 4 = 27m + 41; q(3) = 27 − 12 + m = m + 15. Equating: 27m + 41 = m + 15 ⇒ 26m = −26 ⇒ m = −1.

questions.question: If 4x<sup>3</sup> − 7x<sup>2</sup> + 6x − 3k is exactly divisible by (x + 2), find k.
questions.explanation: p(−2) = −32 − 28 − 12 − 3k = 0 ⇒ −72 − 3k = 0 ⇒ k = −24.

questions.question: Find r if (y + 2) is a factor of 3y<sup>2</sup> − 4ry − 4r<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: p(−2) = 12 + 8r − 4r<sup>2</sup> = 0 ⇒ r<sup>2</sup> − 2r − 3 = 0 ⇒ (r − 3)(r + 1) = 0.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> + x − 1 by (x − 1); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 1; coefficients 1, −1, 1, −1. Row 3: 1, 0, 1 with R = 0.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 by (x + 1); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier −1; coefficients 1, −1, −1, −1. Row 3: 1, −2, 1 with R = −2.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x − 6 by (x + 2); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier −2; coefficients 1, −6, 11, −6. Row 3: 1, −8, 27 with R = −60.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> + 6x<sup>2</sup> − 11x − 6 by (x − 2); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 2; coefficients 1, 6, −11, −6. Row 3: 1, 8, 5 with R = 4.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>4</sup> − x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 by (x + 2); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier −2; coefficients 1, −1, 1, −1, −1. Row 3: 1, −3, 7, −15 with R = 29.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> + x − 1 by (x − 1); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 1; coefficients 1, 1, −1, 1, −1. Row 3: 1, 2, 1, 2 with R = 1.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>5</sup> + x<sup>3</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3 by (x + 3); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier −3; coefficients 1, 0, 1, −2, 0, −3. Row 3: 1, −3, 10, −32, 96 with R = −291.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = x<sup>5</sup> − x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>3</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> + 6x − 6 by (x − 3); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 3; coefficients 1, −1, 1, −3, 6, −6. Row 3: 1, 2, 7, 18, 60 with R = 174.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = 2x<sup>4</sup> − 2x<sup>3</sup> + 100x<sup>2</sup> − 168x + 95 by (x − 2); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 2; coefficients 2, −2, 100, −168, 95. Row 3: 2, 2, 104, 40 with R = 175.

questions.question: By synthetic division divide p(x) = 6x<sup>4</sup> − 72x<sup>3</sup> + 300x<sup>2</sup> − 564x + 270 by (x − 5); find quotient and remainder.
questions.explanation: Multiplier 5; coefficients 6, −72, 300, −564, 270. Row 3: 6, −42, 90, −114 with R = −300.

questions.question: For what value of k is −2 a zero of p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − 14x − k?
questions.explanation: p(−2) = −8 + 4 + 28 − k = 24 − k = 0 ⇒ k = 24.

questions.question: For what value of m is (x − 2) a factor of x<sup>3</sup> + mx<sup>2</sup> − 7x − 10?
questions.explanation: p(2) = 8 + 4m − 14 − 10 = 4m − 16 = 0 ⇒ m = 4.

questions.question: For what value of m is (x + 2) a factor of 4x<sup>3</sup> − 7x<sup>2</sup> + 6x − 3m?
questions.explanation: p(−2) = −32 − 28 − 12 − 3m = −72 − 3m = 0 ⇒ m = −24.

questions.question: For what value of m is −1 a zero of p(x) = 2x<sup>3</sup> − 4mx<sup>2</sup> + x − 1?
questions.explanation: p(−1) = −2 − 4m − 1 − 1 = −4 − 4m = 0 ⇒ m = −1.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> + x − 1 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(1) = 0, so (x − 1) is a factor. Synthetic division by 1 gives q(x) = x<sup>2</sup> + 1.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(1) = 0 gives (x − 1); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 1 = (x + 1)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> − 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x − 6 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(1) = 0 gives (x − 1); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> + 5x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 20 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(−2) = 0 gives (x + 2); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 10 = (x + 5)(x − 2).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup> + 9x − 18 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(2) = 0 gives (x − 2); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> + 9.

questions.question: Factorize 6x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> − x − 2 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(−1) = 0 gives (x + 1); synthetic division gives 6x<sup>2</sup> + x − 2 = (2x − 1)(3x + 2).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> + 8x<sup>2</sup> + 19x + 12 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(−1) = 0 gives (x + 1); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(x + 4).

questions.question: Factorize 2x<sup>3</sup> + 9x<sup>2</sup> + 10x + 3 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(−1) = 0 gives (x + 1); synthetic division gives 2x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 3 = (2x + 1)(x + 3).

questions.question: Factorize x<sup>3</sup> + 12x<sup>2</sup> + 44x + 48 by using factor theorem.
questions.explanation: p(−2) = 0 gives (x + 2); synthetic division gives x<sup>2</sup> + 10x + 24 = (x + 4)(x + 6).

questions.question: State True or False: x<sup>2</sup> + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2).
questions.explanation: (x + 3)(x − 2) = x<sup>2</sup> + x − 6, so the statement is true.

questions.question: State True or False: a<sup>3</sup> + 27 = (a + 3)(a<sup>2</sup> − 3a + 9).
questions.explanation: Sum of two cubes: a<sup>3</sup> + 3<sup>3</sup> = (a + 3)(a<sup>2</sup> − 3a + 9).

questions.question: State True or False: b<sup>3</sup> − 8 = (b − 2)(b<sup>2</sup> + 2b + 4).
questions.explanation: Difference of two cubes: b<sup>3</sup> − 2<sup>3</sup> = (b − 2)(b<sup>2</sup> + 2b + 4).

questions.question: State True or False: a<sup>4</sup> − b<sup>4</sup> = (a − b)(a + b)(a + b)<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: Correct factorization is (a − b)(a + b)(a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>), not (a − b)(a + b)(a + b)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: State True or False: a<sup>6</sup> + b<sup>6</sup> = (a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup>)(a<sup>3</sup> − b<sup>3</sup>).
questions.explanation: a<sup>6</sup> + b<sup>6</sup> = (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>)(a<sup>4</sup> − a<sup>2</sup>b<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>4</sup>); (a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup>)(a<sup>3</sup> − b<sup>3</sup>) = a<sup>6</sup> − b<sup>6</sup>.

questions.question: State True or False: a<sup>5</sup> + b<sup>5</sup> = (a + b)<sup>5</sup>.
questions.explanation: (a + b)<sup>5</sup> expands to a<sup>5</sup> + 5a<sup>4</sup>b + 10a<sup>3</sup>b<sup>2</sup> + …, not a<sup>5</sup> + b<sup>5</sup>.

questions.question: Complete: 16x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>4</sup> = (4x − y<sup>2</sup>) ______.
questions.explanation: Difference of two squares: a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup> = (a − b)(a + b), so the missing factor is 4x + y<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Complete: x<sup>3</sup> − 64y<sup>3</sup> = (x − 4y) ______.
questions.explanation: Difference of two cubes: the second factor is x<sup>2</sup> + (x)(4y) + (4y)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Complete: x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 = (x + 2) ______.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3), so the missing factor is x + 3.

questions.question: Complete: x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = (x − y)<sup>2</sup> ______.
questions.explanation: (x − y)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> − 2xy + y<sup>2</sup>, so x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = (x − y)<sup>2</sup> + 2xy.

questions.question: Complete: a<sup>3</sup> + 27b<sup>3</sup> = (a + 3b) ______.
questions.explanation: Sum of two cubes: the second factor is a<sup>2</sup> − (a)(3b) + (3b)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Factors of a<sup>2</sup> + 2a − 24 are:
questions.explanation: a<sup>2</sup> + 2a − 24 = (a + 6)(a − 4).
questions.optionsRaw: a) a + 4, a − 6  b) a − 4, a + 6  c) a + 3, a − 8  d) a + 8, a − 3

questions.question: Factors of a<sup>2</sup> + 2ab + b<sup>2</sup> − c<sup>2</sup> are:
questions.explanation: (a + b)<sup>2</sup> − c<sup>2</sup> = (a + b + c)(a + b − c).
questions.optionsRaw: a) (a − b + c)(a − b − c)  b) (a + b + c)(a − b − c)  c) (a + b + c)(a + b − c)  d) (a + b + c)(a − b − c)

questions.question: Factors of x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> are:
questions.explanation: Sum of two cubes: x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> = (x + y)(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) (x − y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)  b) (x + y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)  c) (x + y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy − y<sup>2</sup>)  d) (x + y)(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: Factors of y<sup>3</sup> − 27z<sup>3</sup> are:
questions.explanation: Difference of two cubes: y<sup>3</sup> − (3z)<sup>3</sup> = (y − 3z)(y<sup>2</sup> + 3yz + 9z<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) y − 3z, y<sup>2</sup> + 3yz + 9z<sup>2</sup>  b) y − 3z, y + 3z + 9z<sup>2</sup>  c) y − 3z, y<sup>2</sup> − 3yz + 9z<sup>2</sup>  d) y + 3z, y<sup>2</sup> − 3yz + 9z<sup>2</sup>

questions.question: In simplified form 1/(x + y) + y/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>) =
questions.explanation: 1/(x + y) + y/((x − y)(x + y)) = (x − y + y)/((x − y)(x + y)) = x/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) (y + 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  b) x/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  c) y/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  d) (y − 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: Find m so that x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + m is a complete square:
questions.explanation: For a perfect square x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + m, m = (4/2)<sup>2</sup> = 4.
questions.optionsRaw: a) 16  b) −16  c) 4  d) −4

questions.question: Find the HCF of 72x<sup>4</sup>y<sup>5</sup>z<sup>2</sup> and 120x<sup>3</sup>y<sup>6</sup>z<sup>8</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: HCF of 72 and 120 is 24; the lowest powers are x<sup>3</sup>, y<sup>5</sup>, z<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Find the HCF of 18r<sup>3</sup>s<sup>4</sup>t<sup>5</sup>, 120r<sup>4</sup>s<sup>3</sup>t<sup>8</sup> and 210r<sup>7</sup>s<sup>7</sup>t<sup>3</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: HCF of 18, 120, 210 is 6; the lowest powers are r<sup>3</sup>, s<sup>3</sup>, t<sup>3</sup>.

questions.question: Find the HCF of x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 18 and x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 18 = (x − 6)(x + 3) and x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3); common factor (x + 3).

questions.question: Find the HCF of 4x<sup>2</sup> − 9 and 2x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 3 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: 4x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = (2x − 3)(2x + 3) and 2x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 3 = (2x − 3)(x − 1); common factor (2x − 3).

questions.question: Find the HCF of (2a<sup>2</sup> − 8b<sup>2</sup>), (4a<sup>2</sup> + 4ab − 24b<sup>2</sup>) and (2a<sup>2</sup> − 12ab + 16b<sup>2</sup>) by factorization method.
questions.explanation: 2(a − 2b)(a + 2b), 4(a + 3b)(a − 2b) and 2(a − 2b)(a − 4b); common factor 2(a − 2b).

questions.question: Find the HCF of x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> + x + 1 and x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 1 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> + x<sup>2</sup> + x + 1 = (x + 1)(x<sup>2</sup> + 1) and x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 1 = (x + 1)<sup>3</sup>; common factor (x + 1).

questions.question: Find the HCF of x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 2 and 3x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 6 by division method.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 2 = (x + 1)(x + 2); 3x<sup>2</sup> − 3x − 6 = 3(x − 2)(x + 1); common factor (x + 1).

questions.question: Find the HCF of 2x<sup>3</sup> + 15x<sup>2</sup> + 31x + 12 and 6x<sup>3</sup> + 46x<sup>2</sup> + 100x + 48 by division method.
Find the HCF of x<sup>3</sup> − 5x<sup>2</sup> + 10x − 8 and x<sup>3</sup> − 4x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 6 by division method.
questions.explanation: Both polynomials vanish at x = 2, so (x − 2) is their common factor.

questions.question: Find the HCF of x<sup>4</sup> + 3x<sup>3</sup> + 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 1, x<sup>3</sup> + 4x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 1 and x<sup>3</sup> + 5x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 2 by division method.
questions.explanation: Successive division gives the common divisor x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 1.

questions.question: Find the LCM of 27a<sup>4</sup>b<sup>5</sup>c<sup>2</sup> and 81ab<sup>2</sup>c<sup>8</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: LCM of 27 and 81 is 81; the highest powers are a<sup>4</sup>, b<sup>5</sup>, c<sup>8</sup>.

questions.question: Find the LCM of 24p<sup>2</sup>q<sup>3</sup>r<sup>4</sup>, 100p<sup>5</sup>q<sup>4</sup>r<sup>5</sup> and 300p<sup>3</sup>qr<sup>8</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: LCM of 24, 100, 300 is 600; the highest powers are p<sup>5</sup>, q<sup>4</sup>, r<sup>8</sup>.

questions.question: Find the LCM of 21x<sup>2</sup> − 14x and 3x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 2 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: 21x<sup>2</sup> − 14x = 7x(3x − 2) and 3x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 2 = (3x − 2)(x − 1); LCM = 7x(3x − 2)(x − 1).

questions.question: Find the LCM of x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 28 and x<sup>2</sup> + x − 12 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 28 = (x + 4)(x + 7) and x<sup>2</sup> + x − 12 = (x + 4)(x − 3); common factor (x + 4).

questions.question: Find the LCM of 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 3, 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 1 and 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 1 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: 6x<sup>2</sup> + 11x + 3 = (3x + 1)(2x + 3) and 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 1 = (3x + 1)(x − 1); LCM = (3x + 1)(x − 1)(2x + 3).

questions.question: Find the LCM of x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>, x<sup>3</sup> − y<sup>3</sup> and x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup> by factorization method.
questions.answer: LCM = (x + y)(x − y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>)
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> = (x − y)(x + y); x<sup>3</sup> − y<sup>3</sup> = (x − y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>); x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>4</sup> = (x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>).

questions.question: Find the LCM of x<sup>2</sup> − 25x + 100 and x<sup>2</sup> − x − 20 by division method.
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 25x + 100 = (x − 20)(x − 5) and x<sup>2</sup> − x − 20 = (x − 5)(x + 4); LCM = (x − 20)(x − 5)(x + 4).

questions.question: Find the LCM of 3x<sup>2</sup> + 14x + 8 and 6x<sup>2</sup> + x − 2 by division method.
questions.explanation: 3x<sup>2</sup> + 14x + 8 = (3x + 2)(x + 4) and 6x<sup>2</sup> + x − 2 = (3x + 2)(2x − 1); LCM = (3x + 2)(x + 4)(2x − 1).

questions.question: Find the LCM of x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> − z<sup>2</sup> − 2yz and y<sup>2</sup> − z<sup>2</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> − 2xz by division method.
questions.answer: LCM = (x + y + z)(x − y − z)(y − z − x)
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − (y + z)<sup>2</sup> = (x + y + z)(x − y − z) and y<sup>2</sup> − (x + z)<sup>2</sup> = (y + x + z)(y − x − z); LCM is the product of the factors.

questions.question: Find the LCM of 3x<sup>3</sup> + 9x<sup>2</sup> − 84x and 4x<sup>4</sup> − 24x<sup>3</sup> + 32x<sup>2</sup> by division method.
questions.explanation: 3x(x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 28) = 3x(x + 7)(x − 4) and 4x<sup>2</sup>(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 8) = 4x<sup>2</sup>(x − 4)(x − 2); LCM = 12x<sup>3</sup>(x − 4)(x + 7)(x − 2).

questions.question: If the HCF of x<sup>2</sup> − 11x + 24 and x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 6 is (x − 3), find the LCM.
questions.explanation: LCM = (p(x) × q(x))/HCF. With p = (x − 3)(x − 8): LCM = [(x − 3)(x − 8)(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 6)]/(x − 3) = (x − 8)(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 6).

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two expressions are (x + 3) and (x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 15). If one expression is x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 15, find the second expression.
questions.explanation: Second = (HCF × LCM)/first = [(x + 3)(x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 15)]/[(x + 3)(x + 5)] = (x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 15)/(x + 5) = x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 3.

questions.question: The HCF and LCM of two polynomials of the second degree are (3x − 2) and (3x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> − 4). Find the product of the two polynomials.
questions.explanation: Product = HCF × LCM = (3x − 2)(3x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> − 4) = 9x<sup>4</sup> + 15x<sup>3</sup> − 14x<sup>2</sup> − 12x + 8.

questions.question: Verify HCF × LCM = p(x)q(x) for p(x) = x<sup>2</sup> − 8x − 20 and q(x) = x<sup>2</sup> − 15x + 50.
questions.explanation: p = (x − 10)(x + 2), q = (x − 10)(x − 5); HCF = (x − 10), LCM = (x − 10)(x + 2)(x − 5). LCM × HCF = (x − 10)<sup>2</sup>(x + 2)(x − 5) = p × q.

questions.question: A carpenter has wooden planks 12 cm and 18 cm long. He wants to cut them into equal-size planks without wasting wood. What size should he cut them into?
questions.explanation: The required size is HCF(12, 18) = 6 cm.

questions.question: Train A stops at Hyderabad every 12 minutes and train B every 14 minutes; both stop together at 10:30 am. When do they next stop together?
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 14) = 84 minutes = 1 h 24 min. 10:30 am + 1 h 24 min = 11:54 am.

questions.question: Simplify 4x/(x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 1) + 3/(x + 1).
Simplify (3x − 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 1) − (4x<sup>2</sup> − 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 3).
questions.explanation: LCD = (x + 1)<sup>2</sup>(x − 3); numerator = (3x − 1)(x − 3) − (4x<sup>2</sup> − 1)(x + 1) = −4x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> − 9x + 4.

questions.question: Simplify 1/(x + 1) − 2/(x + 2) + 3/(x + 3).
Simplify (x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 3)/5 × 10/(x + 1).
Simplify (x<sup>2</sup> − 4x − 21)/(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x − 7) ÷ (x + 9)/(x + 1).
Simplify [3/(x + 1) + 1/(x + 2)] ÷ [2/(x + 3) − 1].
questions.explanation: Numerator = (4x + 7)/((x + 1)(x + 2)); denominator = (2 − x − 3)/(x + 3) = −(x + 1)/(x + 3). Dividing gives −(x + 3)(4x + 7)/((x + 1)<sup>2</sup>(x + 2)).

questions.question: Simplify (1/(x<sup>2</sup> − 9)) ÷ (1/(x + 3)) − 3/(x − 2).
questions.explanation: (x + 3)/((x − 3)(x + 3)) = 1/(x − 3); then 1/(x − 3) − 3/(x − 2) = [(x − 2) − 3(x − 3)]/((x − 3)(x − 2)) = (−2x + 7)/((x − 2)(x − 3)).

questions.question: Simplify 1/(x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 15) + 1/(x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 12) − 1/(x<sup>2</sup> + x − 12).
questions.explanation: LCD = (x − 3)(x + 3)(x + 4)(x + 5); numerator = (x + 4)(x − 3) + (x − 3)(x + 5) − (x + 3)(x + 5) = x<sup>2</sup> − 5x − 42.

questions.question: Simplify 2[(x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 12)/(x<sup>2</sup> − 16) + (x<sup>2</sup> + x − 2)/(x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 4)] × (x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 8)/(8x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 4).
questions.explanation: Bracket = (x + 3)/(x − 4) + (x − 1)/(x + 2) = 2(x<sup>2</sup> + 5)/((x − 4)(x + 2)); × (x − 4)(x + 2)/(8x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 4) gives 2(x<sup>2</sup> + 5)/(2(4x<sup>2</sup> + x + 2)) × 2 = 2(x<sup>2</sup> + 5)/(4x<sup>2</sup> + x + 2).

questions.question: Find the square root of 36x<sup>2</sup> − 60xy + 25y<sup>2</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: 36x<sup>2</sup> − 60xy + 25y<sup>2</sup> = (6x − 5y)<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is 6x − 5y.

questions.question: Find the square root of 9x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> + 6 by factorization method.
questions.explanation: (3x + 1/x)<sup>2</sup> = 9x<sup>2</sup> + 6 + 1/x<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is 3x + 1/x.

questions.question: Find the square root of 4x<sup>4</sup>y<sup>4</sup> − 12x<sup>3</sup>y<sup>3</sup>/z<sup>2</sup> + 9x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup>/z<sup>4</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: This is (2x<sup>2</sup>y<sup>2</sup> − 3xy/z<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Find the square root of 36(3 − 2x)<sup>2</sup> − 48(3 − 2x)y + 16y<sup>2</sup> by factorization method.
questions.explanation: = [6(3 − 2x) − 4y]<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is 6(3 − 2x) − 4y = 18 − 12x − 4y.

questions.question: Find the square root of (x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>) + 2(x + 1/x) + 3 by factorization method.
Find the square root of (4x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 1)(9x<sup>2</sup> − 54x + 81) by factorization method.
questions.explanation: = (2x − 1)<sup>2</sup>(3x − 9)<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is (2x − 1)(3x − 9) = 3(2x − 1)(x − 3).

questions.question: Find the square root of (x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 1)(x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 9) by factorization method.
questions.explanation: = (x − 1)<sup>2</sup>(x − 3)<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is (x − 1)(x − 3).

questions.question: Find the square root of (x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 15)(x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 10)(x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6) by factorization method.
Find the square root of x<sup>4</sup> + 2x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 1 by division method.
questions.explanation: (x<sup>2</sup> + x + 1)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>4</sup> + 2x<sup>3</sup> + 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 1.

questions.question: Find the square root of 25x<sup>4</sup> + 40x<sup>3</sup> + 26x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 1 by division method.
questions.explanation: (5x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 25x<sup>4</sup> + 40x<sup>3</sup> + 26x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 1.

questions.question: Find the square root of 4x<sup>4</sup> + 8x<sup>3</sup> + 20x<sup>2</sup> + 16x + 16 by division method.
questions.explanation: (2x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 4x<sup>4</sup> + 8x<sup>3</sup> + 20x<sup>2</sup> + 16x + 16.

questions.question: Find the square root of x<sup>2</sup>/y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/x<sup>2</sup> + 47 − 14y/x + 14x/y by division method.
questions.explanation: (x/y + 7 − y/x)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup>/y<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/x<sup>2</sup> + 47 − 14y/x + 14x/y.

questions.question: Find the square root of x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 3 − 2/x + 1/x<sup>2</sup> by division method.
questions.explanation: (x − 1 + 1/x)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 3 − 2/x + 1/x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Find the square root of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/9 + 9z<sup>2</sup> + 2xy/3 + 2yz + 6xz by division method.
questions.explanation: (x + y/3 + 3z)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/9 + 9z<sup>2</sup> + 2xy/3 + 2yz + 6xz.

questions.question: Find the square root of (x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>2</sup> − 8(x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup>) + 16 by division method.
questions.explanation: = (x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> − 4)<sup>2</sup>, so the square root is x<sup>2</sup> − 4 + 1/x<sup>2</sup>.

questions.question: Find the square root of x<sup>6</sup> + 1/x<sup>6</sup> − 4(x<sup>3</sup> + 1/x<sup>3</sup>) + 6 (x ≠ 0) by division method.
questions.explanation: (x<sup>3</sup> − 2 + 1/x<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>6</sup> + 1/x<sup>6</sup> − 4(x<sup>3</sup> + 1/x<sup>3</sup>) + 6.

questions.question: What should be added to 4x<sup>4</sup> + 4x<sup>3</sup> + 17x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 9 to make it a perfect square?
questions.explanation: (2x<sup>2</sup> + x + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 4x<sup>4</sup> + 4x<sup>3</sup> + 17x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 16; we have 9, so add 7.

questions.question: What should be subtracted from 9x<sup>6</sup> − 12x<sup>5</sup> + 4x<sup>4</sup> − 18x<sup>3</sup> − 12x<sup>2</sup> + 18 to make it a perfect square?
questions.explanation: The perfect square is (3x<sup>3</sup> − 2x<sup>2</sup> − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 9x<sup>6</sup> − 12x<sup>5</sup> + 4x<sup>4</sup> − 18x<sup>3</sup> + 12x<sup>2</sup> + 9; the difference is −24x<sup>2</sup> + 9.

questions.question: For what value of m is 9x<sup>4</sup> + 12x<sup>3</sup> + 34x<sup>2</sup> + mx + 25 a perfect square?
questions.explanation: (3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 5)<sup>2</sup> = 9x<sup>4</sup> + 12x<sup>3</sup> + 34x<sup>2</sup> + 20x + 25, so m = 20.

questions.question: For what values of p and q is x<sup>4</sup> + 8x<sup>3</sup> + 30x<sup>2</sup> + px + q a perfect square?
questions.explanation: (x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 7)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>4</sup> + 8x<sup>3</sup> + 30x<sup>2</sup> + 56x + 49, so p = 56 and q = 49.

questions.question: For what values of a and b is x<sup>4</sup> + 4x<sup>3</sup> + 10x<sup>2</sup> + ax + b a perfect square?
questions.explanation: (x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 3)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>4</sup> + 4x<sup>3</sup> + 10x<sup>2</sup> + 12x + 9, so a = 12 and b = 9.

questions.question: State True or False: HCF of y<sup>2</sup> − 4 and y − 2 is y − 2.
questions.explanation: y<sup>2</sup> − 4 = (y − 2)(y + 2) and (y − 2) divides it, so HCF is y − 2.

questions.question: State True or False: HCF of a<sup>3</sup> − 1 and a<sup>2</sup> − 1 is a + 1.
questions.explanation: a<sup>3</sup> − 1 = (a − 1)(a<sup>2</sup> + a + 1) and a<sup>2</sup> − 1 = (a − 1)(a + 1); HCF is (a − 1).

questions.question: State True or False: LCM of x<sup>3</sup> + 1 and x + 1 is x<sup>3</sup> + 1.
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> + 1 = (x + 1)(x<sup>2</sup> − x + 1), so LCM = x<sup>3</sup> + 1.

questions.question: State True or False: LCM of x<sup>4</sup> − y<sup>4</sup> and x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> is x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>.
questions.explanation: x<sup>4</sup> − y<sup>4</sup> = (x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)(x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>), so LCM = x<sup>4</sup> − y<sup>4</sup>.

questions.question: State True or False: HCF of a<sup>2</sup> + 4a + 3 and a<sup>2</sup> + 5a + 6 is a + 3.
Fill in the blank: There are ______ methods for finding the HCF of polynomials.
questions.explanation: Factorization method and division method.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: LCM × HCF of two polynomials p(x) and q(x) = ______.
questions.explanation: Fundamental relation: LCM × HCF = product of the polynomials.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: HCF of y<sup>2</sup> − 5y, y + 6 and y − 2 is ______.
questions.explanation: The three expressions have no common factor, so their HCF is 1.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: LCM of y<sup>2</sup> + 3y + 2 and y<sup>2</sup> + 5y + 6 is ______.
Fill in the blank: HCF of y<sup>2</sup> − 1/y<sup>2</sup> and y + 1/y is ______.
questions.explanation: y<sup>2</sup> − 1/y<sup>2</sup> = (y − 1/y)(y + 1/y), so the HCF is y + 1/y.

questions.question: HCF of x<sup>3</sup> − 8y<sup>3</sup> and x<sup>2</sup> − 4xy + 4y<sup>2</sup> is:
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> − 8y<sup>3</sup> = (x − 2y)(x<sup>2</sup> + 2xy + 4y<sup>2</sup>) and x<sup>2</sup> − 4xy + 4y<sup>2</sup> = (x − 2y)<sup>2</sup>; HCF = (x − 2y).
questions.optionsRaw: a) x − 4y  b) x<sup>2</sup> + 2xy + y<sup>2</sup>  c) x + 2y  d) x − 2y

questions.question: LCM of (2y + 3z)<sup>5</sup> and (2y + 3z)<sup>3</sup> is:
questions.explanation: LCM takes the highest power, so (2y + 3z)<sup>5</sup>.
questions.optionsRaw: a) (2y + 3z)<sup>8</sup>  b) (2y + 3z)<sup>3</sup>  c) (2y + 3z)<sup>2</sup>  d) (2y + 3z)<sup>5</sup>

questions.question: HCF of x<sup>3</sup> − y<sup>3</sup> and x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup> is:
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> − y<sup>3</sup> = (x − y)(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>); the common factor is x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>.
questions.optionsRaw: a) x + y  b) x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>  c) x − y  d) (x − y)<sup>2</sup>

questions.question: LCM of (x − y)<sup>4</sup> and (x − y)<sup>3</sup> is:
questions.explanation: LCM takes the highest power, so (x − y)<sup>4</sup>.
questions.optionsRaw: a) (x − y)  b) (x − y)<sup>3</sup>  c) (x − y)<sup>4</sup>  d) (x − y)<sup>7</sup>

questions.question: Simplified form of 1/(x + y) + y/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>) is:
questions.explanation: = 1/(x + y) + y/((x − y)(x + y)) = (x − y + y)/((x − y)(x + y)) = x/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) (y + 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  b) x/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  c) y/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  d) (x + y)/(x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: Simplified form of y/(25x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>) − 1/(5x − y) is:
questions.explanation: = [y − (5x + y)]/((5x − y)(5x + y)) = −5x/(25x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) 5x/(25x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)  b) 5x/(5x − y)  c) −5x/(5x + y)  d) −5x/(25x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: (a<sup>3</sup>x<sup>3</sup> + a<sup>3</sup>y<sup>3</sup>)/(a<sup>2</sup>(x + y)) =
questions.explanation: = a<sup>3</sup>(x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup>)/(a<sup>2</sup>(x + y)) = a(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>) after cancelling (x + y).
questions.optionsRaw: a) ax<sup>2</sup> + ay<sup>2</sup>  b) x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>  c) a(x<sup>2</sup> − xy + y<sup>2</sup>)  d) a(x<sup>2</sup> + xy + y<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: a/(a − b) − b/(a + b) =
questions.explanation: = [a(a + b) − b(a − b)]/(a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>) = (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>)/(a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>).
questions.optionsRaw: a) (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>)/(a − b)  b) (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>)/(a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>)  c) (a + b)/(a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>)  d) (a − b)/(a<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup>)

questions.question: LCM = ______, given that p and q are any two polynomials:
questions.explanation: From LCM × HCF = p × q, LCM = (p × q)/HCF.
questions.optionsRaw: a) HCF/(p × q)  b) (p × q)/HCF  c) p/HCF  d) q/HCF

questions.question: LCM of x<sup>2</sup> − x + 1 and x<sup>3</sup> + 1 is:
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> + 1 = (x + 1)(x<sup>2</sup> − x + 1), so LCM = x<sup>3</sup> + 1.
questions.optionsRaw: a) x + 1  b) x<sup>2</sup> − x + 1  c) x<sup>3</sup> + 1  d) x<sup>2</sup> + x + 1

questions.question: Solve the equation: ¼x = 5
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 4: x = 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.question: Solve the equation: x/4 = −3
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 4: x = −3 × 4 = −12.

questions.question: Solve the equation: −5 = −x/6
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by −6: x = (−5)(−6) = 30.

questions.question: Solve the equation: −x/8 = −5
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by −8: x = (−5)(−8) = 40.

questions.question: Solve the equation: y − 2/5 = −1/3
Solve the equation: 2y − 3/5 = 1/2
Solve the equation: (2x − 4)/5 = (5x − 12)/4
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 4(2x − 4) = 5(5x − 12) ⇒ 8x − 16 = 25x − 60 ⇒ 44 = 17x ⇒ x = 44/17.

questions.question: Solve the equation: 3x/5 + 7 = 2x/3
questions.explanation: Multiply by 15: 9x + 105 = 10x ⇒ x = 105.

questions.question: Solve the equation: 3x/5 + 7 = 2x/3 + 4x/5
questions.explanation: Multiply by 15: 9x + 105 = 10x + 12x = 22x ⇒ 105 = 13x ⇒ x = 105/13.

questions.question: Solve the equation: 6/(2x − 5) − 4/(x − 3) = 0
questions.explanation: 6/(2x − 5) = 4/(x − 3) ⇒ 6(x − 3) = 4(2x − 5) ⇒ 6x − 18 = 8x − 20 ⇒ 2 = 2x ⇒ x = 1.

questions.question: Solve the equation: (7x − 4)/15 = (7x + 4)/10
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 10(7x − 4) = 15(7x + 4) ⇒ 70x − 40 = 105x + 60 ⇒ −100 = 35x ⇒ x = −20/7.

questions.question: Solve the equation: (3x − 2)/10 = (7x − 3)/15 − 2
questions.explanation: Multiply by 30: 3(3x − 2) = 2(7x − 3) − 60 ⇒ 9x − 6 = 14x − 66 ⇒ 60 = 5x ⇒ x = 12.

questions.question: Solve the equation: (12x − 3)/12 = (12x + 3)/8
questions.explanation: Multiply by 24: 2(12x − 3) = 3(12x + 3) ⇒ 24x − 6 = 36x + 9 ⇒ −15 = 12x ⇒ x = −5/4.

questions.question: Solve the equation: ¼x + x = −3 + ½x
questions.explanation: (5/4)x − (1/2)x = −3 ⇒ (3/4)x = −3 ⇒ x = −4.

questions.question: Solve the equation: 1/3 + 2m = m − 3/2
questions.explanation: 2m − m = −3/2 − 1/3 = (−9 − 2)/6 = −11/6 ⇒ m = −11/6.

questions.question: When 25 is added to a number, the result is halved; the answer is 3 times the original number. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. Then (x + 25)/2 = 3x ⇒ x + 25 = 6x ⇒ 25 = 5x ⇒ x = 5. Solution set {5}.

questions.question: When a number is added to 4, the result is equal to subtracting 10 from 3 times of it. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. Then x + 4 = 3x − 10 ⇒ 14 = 2x ⇒ x = 7.

questions.question: Bilal is 6 years older than Ali. Five years from now the sum of their ages will be 40. How old are both of them?
questions.explanation: Let Ali = a, Bilal = a + 6. Five years later: (a + 5) + (a + 6 + 5) = 40 ⇒ 2a + 16 = 40 ⇒ a = 12. So Ali = 12, Bilal = 18.

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: 6 + √x = 7
questions.explanation: √x = 1 ⇒ x = 1. Check: 6 + √1 = 6 + 1 = 7. ✓

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √(x − 9) = 1
questions.explanation: Squaring: x − 9 = 1 ⇒ x = 10. Check: √(10 − 9) = 1. ✓

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √(y/4) − 2 = 3
questions.explanation: √(y/4) = 5 ⇒ y/4 = 25 ⇒ y = 100. Check: √(100/4) − 2 = 5 − 2 = 3. ✓

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √(4x + 5) = √(3x − 7)
questions.explanation: Squaring: 4x + 5 = 3x − 7 ⇒ x = −12.

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √(3y + 12)/7 = 3
Find the solution set and verify: √x + 9 = 7
questions.explanation: √x = −2, impossible since a square root is non-negative. Hence the solution set is empty.

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √(25y − 50) = √(y − 2)
questions.explanation: Squaring: 25y − 50 = y − 2 ⇒ 24y = 48 ⇒ y = 2. Check: √0 = √0. ✓

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: √x − 8 = 1
questions.explanation: √x = 9 ⇒ x = 81. Check: √81 − 8 = 9 − 8 = 1. ✓

questions.question: Find the solution set and verify: 10√(x + 20) = 100
Find the solution set: |2x + 1| = 6
questions.explanation: 2x + 1 = 6 ⇒ x = 5/2; 2x + 1 = −6 ⇒ x = −7/2.

questions.question: Find the solution set, x ∈ W: |5x − 12| = 7
questions.explanation: 5x − 12 = 7 ⇒ x = 19/5 ∉ W; 5x − 12 = −7 ⇒ x = 1 ∈ W.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |2x/7| = 12
questions.explanation: 2x/7 = 12 ⇒ x = 42; 2x/7 = −12 ⇒ x = −42.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |(2x + 1)/3| = 8
Find the solution set, x ∈ N: |5x − 3| − 8 = 4
questions.explanation: |5x − 3| = 12 ⇒ 5x − 3 = 12 ⇒ x = 3 ∈ N; or 5x − 3 = −12 ⇒ x = −9/5 ∉ N.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |(5x + 1)/7| − 3 = 8
Find the solution set: |(2x + 3)/4| + 2 = 7
Find the solution set, x ∈ Z: |(3x + 6)/12| + 1 = 3
questions.explanation: |(3x + 6)/12| = 2 ⇒ 3x + 6 = 24 ⇒ x = 6; or 3x + 6 = −24 ⇒ x = −10.

questions.question: Find the solution set: 3/2 = |7x + 8|
questions.explanation: 7x + 8 = 3/2 ⇒ 7x = −13/2 ⇒ x = −13/14; or 7x + 8 = −3/2 ⇒ 7x = −19/2 ⇒ x = −19/14.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |(2x − 3)/5| − 12 = 5
questions.explanation: |(2x − 3)/5| = 17 ⇒ 2x − 3 = 85 ⇒ x = 44; or 2x − 3 = −85 ⇒ x = −41.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |3x + 1| + 1 = 3/4
questions.explanation: |3x + 1| = 3/4 − 1 = −1/4, impossible since modulus is non-negative. Hence the solution set is empty.

questions.question: Find the solution set: |(2x + 1)/7| = 1
questions.explanation: (2x + 1)/7 = 1 ⇒ 2x + 1 = 7 ⇒ x = 3; or (2x + 1)/7 = −1 ⇒ 2x + 1 = −7 ⇒ x = −4.

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: 2x − 7 > 6 + x, ∀ x ∈ N
questions.explanation: 2x − x > 6 + 7 ⇒ x > 13. Since x ∈ N, the solution set is {14, 15, 16, …} (open circle at 13, arrow to the right).

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: 7x − 6 > 3x + 10, ∀ x ∈ &8477;
questions.explanation: 7x − 3x > 10 + 6 ⇒ 4x > 16 ⇒ x > 4. Solution set {x | x ∈ &8477; ∧ x > 4} (open circle at 4, arrow to the right).

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: (y + 5)/20 < (25 − 4y)/10, ∀ y ∈ N
questions.explanation: Multiply by 20: y + 5 < 2(25 − 4y) ⇒ y + 5 < 50 − 8y ⇒ 9y < 45 ⇒ y < 5. Since y ∈ N, the solution set is {1, 2, 3, 4}.

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: |2x + 3| < x + 2, ∀ x ∈ Z
questions.explanation: For |2x + 3| < x + 2 we need x + 2 > 0 ⇒ x > −2. Then −(x + 2) < 2x + 3 < x + 2: from 2x + 3 < x + 2, x < −1; from 2x + 3 > −x − 2, 3x > −5 ⇒ x > −5/3. No integer satisfies both, so the solution set is empty.

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: |2y + 8| < 11, ∀ y ∈ &8477;
questions.explanation: −11 < 2y + 8 < 11 ⇒ −19 < 2y < 3 ⇒ −19/2 < y < 3/2. Solution set {y | y ∈ &8477; ∧ −19/2 < y < 3/2} (open circles at both ends).

questions.question: Find the solution set and illustrate on the number line: 5(2y − 3) > 6(y − 8), ∀ y ∈ &8477;
questions.explanation: 10y − 15 > 6y − 48 ⇒ 4y > −33 ⇒ y > −33/4. Solution set {y | y ∈ &8477; ∧ y > −33/4} (open circle at −33/4, arrow to the right).

questions.question: Ali scored 66 and 72 marks respectively for his two tests. What is the lowest mark he must score in his third test if an average score of at least 75 is required to qualify for a bonus prize?
questions.explanation: Let the third-test score be x. (66 + 72 + x)/3 ≥ 75 ⇒ 138 + x ≥ 225 ⇒ x ≥ 87. Hence Ali must score at least 87 to qualify.

questions.question: Seven less than three times a number and 5 is at least 10. Find all the numbers that satisfy this condition.
questions.explanation: Let the required number be x. Three times the number increased by 5, less 7, is at least 10: 3x + 5 − 7 ≥ 10 ⇒ 3x − 2 ≥ 10 ⇒ 3x ≥ 12 ⇒ x ≥ 4. Hence every number greater than or equal to 4 satisfies the condition.

questions.question: True / False: ay + b = 0, where a = 0, is a linear equation.
questions.explanation: For a linear equation the coefficient of the variable must be non-zero; here a = 0, so it is not a linear equation.

questions.question: True / False: The solution set of 3y − 2 < 7, y ∈ N is {4, 5, 6, …}.
questions.explanation: 3y − 2 < 7 ⇒ 3y < 9 ⇒ y < 3, so with y ∈ N the solution set is {1, 2}, not {4, 5, 6, …}.

questions.question: True / False: The solution set of √y + 1 = 3 is {4}.
questions.explanation: √y = 2 ⇒ y = 4. So the solution set is {4}.

questions.question: True / False: The solution set of |4y| = 8 is {2, −2}.
questions.explanation: |4y| = 8 ⇒ 4y = ±8 ⇒ y = ±2. So the solution set is {2, −2}.

questions.question: True / False: The solution set of −2 ≤ x ≤ 2, x ∈ Z is {−2, 0, 2}.
questions.explanation: The integers from −2 to 2 are {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}; the set {−2, 0, 2} omits −1 and 1, so the statement is false.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The solution set of 2y = −y is __________.
questions.explanation: 2y = −y ⇒ 3y = 0 ⇒ y = 0. Solution set {0}.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The solution set of √(y + 5) = 5 is __________.
questions.explanation: Squaring: y + 5 = 25 ⇒ y = 20. Solution set {20}.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The solution set of |x| − 4 = 0 is __________.
questions.explanation: |x| = 4 ⇒ x = ±4. Solution set {±4} = {−4, 4}.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The solution set of √(x + 5) + 2 = 4 is __________.
questions.explanation: √(x + 5) = 2 ⇒ x + 5 = 4 ⇒ x = −1. Solution set {−1}.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The solution set of 0 < y + 2 < 5 when y ∈ &8477; is __________.
questions.explanation: 0 < y + 2 < 5 ⇒ −2 < y < 3. Solution set {y | y ∈ &8477; ∧ −2 < y < 3}.

questions.explanation: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one solution.

questions.question: The solution set of √(5y + 5) + 5 = 10 is:

questions.question: The solution set of |−y| = 0 is:
questions.explanation: |−y| = 0 ⇒ y = 0. Solution set {0}.

questions.question: If x > 0, y > 0 and x − y < 0, then which of the following relations holds good?
questions.explanation: x − y < 0 ⇒ x < y. Hence x < y holds good.

questions.question: Construct the table for some values of x and y of the linear equation x + y − 2 = 0.
questions.explanation: From x + y − 2 = 0 we get y = 2 − x. Substituting the x-values gives the corresponding y-values.

questions.question: Construct the table for some values of x and y of the linear equation 2x − y − 2 = 4.
questions.explanation: 2x − y − 2 = 4 ⇒ 2x − y = 6 ⇒ y = 2x − 6. Substituting the x-values gives the y-values.

questions.question: Construct the table for some values of x and y of the linear equation ½(x + 2y) − 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: ½(x + 2y) − 6 = 0 ⇒ x + 2y = 12 ⇒ x = 12 − 2y. Substituting the y-values gives the x-values.

questions.question: Construct the table for some values of x and y of the linear equation ⅔(x − 2y) = −2.
questions.explanation: ⅔(x − 2y) = −2 ⇒ x − 2y = −3 ⇒ x = 2y − 3. Substituting the y-values gives the x-values.

questions.question: Construct a table for the equation x + y = 6, satisfying the pair of values.
questions.explanation: From x + y = 6 we get y = 6 − x (equivalently x = 6 − y). Substituting values gives the table of ordered pairs.

questions.question: Plot the graph of: x = 3.5
questions.answer: Vertical line x = 3.5, parallel to the y-axis.
questions.explanation: x = 3.5 for every y, so the graph is a vertical line passing through (3.5, 0).

questions.explanation: −y = 2x ⇒ y = −2x, a straight line passing through the origin.

questions.question: Find the missing coordinates for x − 3y = 6: (3, ?) and (?, −1).
questions.explanation: 3 − 3y = 6 ⇒ −3y = 3 ⇒ y = −1; x − 3(−1) = 6 ⇒ x = 3.

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 3x − 11 = y and x − 3y = 9.
questions.explanation: y = 3x − 11 and x − 3y = 9. Substituting gives x − 3(3x − 11) = 9 ⇒ −8x = −24 ⇒ x = 3, y = −2. The two lines intersect at (3, −2).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: x + y = 4 and 2x − 1 = 5y.
questions.explanation: y = 4 − x and y = (2x − 1)/5. Solving gives x = 3, y = 1; the lines intersect at (3, 1).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 2x = y + 5 and x = 2y + 1.
questions.explanation: y = 2x − 5 and x = 2y + 1. Substituting gives 2(2y + 1) = y + 5 ⇒ 3y = 3 ⇒ y = 1, x = 3. Intersection (3, 1).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: y = 3x − 5 and x + y = 11.
questions.explanation: x + (3x − 5) = 11 ⇒ 4x = 16 ⇒ x = 4, y = 7. Intersection (4, 7).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 2x + y = 3 and x − y = 0.
questions.explanation: x − y = 0 ⇒ x = y; then 2y + y = 3 ⇒ y = 1, x = 1. Intersection (1, 1).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 2x + 2 = y and y = x − 1.
questions.explanation: 2x + 2 = x − 1 ⇒ x = −3, y = −4. Intersection (−3, −4).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 5 = x + 4y and 2x + 3y = 0.
questions.explanation: x = 5 − 4y; 2(5 − 4y) + 3y = 0 ⇒ 10 − 5y = 0 ⇒ y = 2, x = −3. Intersection (−3, 2).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 3x = 5y − 2 and 3x + 5y = 8.
questions.explanation: Substituting 3x = 5y − 2 into 3x + 5y = 8 gives 10y = 10 ⇒ y = 1, x = 1. Intersection (1, 1).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: (x + 2)/5 + y = 6 and y = 2x − 12.
questions.explanation: (x + 2)/5 + (2x − 12) = 6 ⇒ x + 2 + 10x − 60 = 30 ⇒ 11x = 88 ⇒ x = 8, y = 4. Intersection (8, 4).

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations by graphical method: 3x − 2y = 13 and 2x + 3y = 13.
questions.explanation: Elimination gives 13x = 65 ⇒ x = 5, then y = 1. Intersection (5, 1).

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> + 2x + 3x + 6 = 0 ⇒ x(x + 2) + 3(x + 2) = 0 ⇒ (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0. Hence x = −2 or x = −3.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: 6x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: 6x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 = 0 ⇒ 6x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 2x − 1 = 0 ⇒ 3x(2x − 1) + 1(2x − 1) = 0 ⇒ (2x − 1)(3x + 1) = 0. Hence x = 1/2 or x = −1/3.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: x<sup>2</sup> − 11x + 30 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 11x + 30 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 6x − 5x + 30 = 0 ⇒ x(x − 6) − 5(x − 6) = 0 ⇒ (x − 6)(x − 5) = 0. Hence x = 6 or x = 5.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x = 0 ⇒ x(x − 2) = 0. Hence x = 0 or x = 2.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 15 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 15 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 5x + 3x − 15 = 0 ⇒ x(x − 5) + 3(x − 5) = 0 ⇒ (x − 5)(x + 3) = 0. Hence x = 5 or x = −3.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: 12x<sup>2</sup> − 41x + 24 = 0
questions.explanation: 12x<sup>2</sup> − 41x + 24 = 0 ⇒ 12x<sup>2</sup> − 32x − 9x + 24 = 0 ⇒ 4x(3x − 8) − 3(3x − 8) = 0 ⇒ (3x − 8)(4x − 3) = 0. Hence x = 8/3 or x = 3/4.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: (x − 5)<sup>2</sup> − 9 = 0
questions.explanation: (x − 5)<sup>2</sup> − 9 = 0 ⇒ (x − 5)<sup>2</sup> = 9 ⇒ x − 5 = ±3. Hence x = 8 or x = 2.

questions.question: Solve the equation by factorization: (3x + 4)<sup>2</sup> − 16 = 0
questions.explanation: (3x + 4)<sup>2</sup> − 16 = 0 ⇒ (3x + 4)<sup>2</sup> = 16 ⇒ 3x + 4 = ±4. Hence 3x = 0 ⇒ x = 0, or 3x = −8 ⇒ x = −8/3.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: x<sup>2</sup> + 6x + 1 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 6x = −1. Adding (3)<sup>2</sup>: x<sup>2</sup> + 6x + 9 = −1 + 9 ⇒ (x + 3)<sup>2</sup> = 8 ⇒ x + 3 = ±2√2. Hence x = −3 ± 2√2.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: (3x + 2)(x + 2) = 6 − 2(x + 1)
questions.explanation: (3x + 2)(x + 2) = 6 − 2(x + 1) ⇒ 3x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 4 = 4 − 2x ⇒ 3x<sup>2</sup> + 10x = 0 ⇒ x(3x + 10) = 0. Hence x = 0 or x = −10/3.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: 3x<sup>2</sup> − 8x = −1
questions.explanation: 3x<sup>2</sup> − 8x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − (8/3)x = −1/3. Adding (4/3)<sup>2</sup>: (x − 4/3)<sup>2</sup> = −1/3 + 16/9 = 13/9 ⇒ x − 4/3 = ±√13/3. Hence x = (4 ± √13)/3.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: 24x<sup>2</sup> = −10x + 21
questions.explanation: 24x<sup>2</sup> + 10x − 21 = 0. Dividing by 24: x<sup>2</sup> + (5/12)x = 7/8. Adding (5/24)<sup>2</sup>: (x + 5/24)<sup>2</sup> = 7/8 + 25/576 = 529/576 ⇒ x + 5/24 = ±23/24. Hence x = 3/4 or x = −7/6.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: 2(x<sup>2</sup> − 3) − 3x = 2(x + 3)
questions.explanation: 2x<sup>2</sup> − 6 − 3x = 2x + 6 ⇒ 2x<sup>2</sup> − 5x − 12 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − (5/2)x = 6. Adding (5/4)<sup>2</sup>: (x − 5/4)<sup>2</sup> = 6 + 25/16 = 121/16 ⇒ x − 5/4 = ±11/4. Hence x = 4 or x = −3/2.

questions.question: Solve by completing the square: 2x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 2x = 1/2. Adding (1)<sup>2</sup>: (x + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 3/2 ⇒ x + 1 = ±√(3/2) = ±√6/2. Hence x = (−2 ± √6)/2.

questions.question: If 2 is a root of the equation 3x<sup>2</sup> + bx − 8 = 0, find the value of b.
questions.explanation: Putting x = 2: 3(2)<sup>2</sup> + b(2) − 8 = 0 ⇒ 12 + 2b − 8 = 0 ⇒ 2b = −4 ⇒ b = −2.

questions.question: If 2 is a root of the equation 3x<sup>2</sup> + bx − 8 = 0, find the other root.
questions.explanation: With b = −2 the equation is 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 8 = 0. Product of roots = −8/3; one root is 2, so the other is (−8/3)/2 = −4/3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x = 15
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 15 = 0; a = 1, b = −2, c = −15. x = [2 ± √(4 + 60)]/2 = [2 ± 8]/2. Hence x = 5 or x = −3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 10x<sup>2</sup> + 19x − 15 = 0
questions.explanation: a = 10, b = 19, c = −15. x = [−19 ± √(361 + 600)]/20 = [−19 ± 31]/20. Hence x = 12/20 = 3/5 or x = −50/20 = −5/2.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: x<sup>2</sup> = −x + 1
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + x − 1 = 0; a = 1, b = 1, c = −1. x = [−1 ± √(1 + 4)]/2 = (−1 ± √5)/2.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 2x = 9 − 3x<sup>2</sup>
questions.explanation: 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 9 = 0; a = 3, b = 2, c = −9. x = [−2 ± √(4 + 108)]/6 = [−2 ± 4√7]/6 = (−1 ± 2√7)/3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 9x<sup>2</sup> = 12x − 49
questions.explanation: 9x<sup>2</sup> − 12x + 49 = 0; a = 9, b = −12, c = 49. Discriminant = 144 − 1764 = −1620 < 0, so x = [12 ± √(−1620)]/18 = [12 ± 18√5 i]/18 = (2 ± 3√5 i)/3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: ½x<sup>2</sup> + ¾x − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 4: 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 4 = 0; a = 2, b = 3, c = −4. x = [−3 ± √(9 + 32)]/4 = (−3 ± √41)/4.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 3x<sup>2</sup> − 2x + 2 = 0
questions.explanation: a = 3, b = −2, c = 2. Discriminant = 4 − 24 = −20 < 0, so x = [2 ± √(−20)]/6 = [2 ± 2√5 i]/6 = (1 ± √5 i)/3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 6x<sup>2</sup> − x − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: a = 6, b = −1, c = −1. x = [1 ± √(1 + 24)]/12 = [1 ± 5]/12. Hence x = 6/12 = 1/2 or x = −4/12 = −1/3.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 4x<sup>2</sup> − 10x = 0
questions.explanation: x(4x − 10) = 0. Hence x = 0 or x = 10/4 = 5/2.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: x<sup>2</sup> − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> = 1 ⇒ x = ±1. Hence x = 1 or x = −1.

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: x<sup>2</sup> − 6x + 9 = 0
questions.explanation: (x − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 0, so x = 3 (a repeated root).

questions.question: Solve by the quadratic formula: 1/(x + 4) − 1/(x − 4) = 4
questions.explanation: [(x − 4) − (x + 4)]/((x + 4)(x − 4)) = 4 ⇒ −8/(x<sup>2</sup> − 16) = 4 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 16 = −2 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> = 14. Hence x = ±√14.

questions.question: Solve: x<sup>4</sup> − 8x<sup>2</sup> − 9 = 0
questions.explanation: Let y = x<sup>2</sup>: y<sup>2</sup> − 8y − 9 = 0 ⇒ (y − 9)(y + 1) = 0 ⇒ y = 9 or y = −1. Thus x<sup>2</sup> = 9 ⇒ x = ±3, and x<sup>2</sup> = −1 ⇒ x = ±i.

questions.question: Solve: x<sup>4</sup> − 3x<sup>2</sup> − 4 = 0
questions.explanation: Let y = x<sup>2</sup>: y<sup>2</sup> − 3y − 4 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y + 1) = 0 ⇒ y = 4 or y = −1. Thus x<sup>2</sup> = 4 ⇒ x = ±2, and x<sup>2</sup> = −1 ⇒ x = ±i.

questions.question: Solve: 12x<sup>4</sup> − 11x<sup>2</sup> + 2 = 0
questions.explanation: Let y = x<sup>2</sup>: 12y<sup>2</sup> − 11y + 2 = 0 ⇒ (3y − 2)(4y − 1) = 0 ⇒ y = 2/3 or y = 1/4. Thus x<sup>2</sup> = 2/3 ⇒ x = ±√6/3, and x<sup>2</sup> = 1/4 ⇒ x = ±1/2.

questions.question: Solve: (2x + 3)/(x + 1) + 6(x + 1)/(2x + 3) = 7
questions.explanation: Let y = (2x + 3)/(x + 1); then y + 6/y = 7 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> − 7y + 6 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 1) = 0. If y = 6: (2x + 3)/(x + 1) = 6 ⇒ 2x + 3 = 6x + 6 ⇒ x = −3/4. If y = 1: (2x + 3)/(x + 1) = 1 ⇒ 2x + 3 = x + 1 ⇒ x = −2.

questions.question: Solve: √((2x<sup>2</sup> + 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> + 1)) + 6√((x<sup>2</sup> + 1)/(2x<sup>2</sup> + 1)) = 5
questions.explanation: Let y = √((2x<sup>2</sup> + 1)/(x<sup>2</sup> + 1)); then y + 6/y = 5 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> − 5y + 6 = 0 ⇒ y = 2 or y = 3. This gives 2x<sup>2</sup> + 1 = 2(x<sup>2</sup> + 1) (impossible) or 2x<sup>2</sup> + 1 = 9(x<sup>2</sup> + 1) ⇒ 7x<sup>2</sup> = −8 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> = −8/7 ⇒ x = ±2√14 i/7. (The y = 2 branch yields x<sup>2</sup> = −1/2 ⇒ x = ±√6 i/2.)

questions.question: Solve: 5<sup>x + 1</sup> + 5<sup>2 − x</sup> = 5<sup>3</sup> + 1
questions.explanation: Write 5<sup>x + 1</sup> = 5·5<sup>x</sup> and 5<sup>2 − x</sup> = 25/5<sup>x</sup>. Let y = 5<sup>x</sup>: 5y + 25/y = 126 ⇒ 5y<sup>2</sup> − 126y + 25 = 0 ⇒ (5y − 1)(y − 25) = 0 ⇒ y = 1/5 or y = 25. So 5<sup>x</sup> = 5<sup>−1</sup> ⇒ x = −1, or 5<sup>x</sup> = 5<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x = 2.

questions.question: Solve: 2<sup>x</sup> + 16/2<sup>x</sup> = 8
questions.explanation: Let y = 2<sup>x</sup>: y + 16/y = 8 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> − 8y + 16 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)<sup>2</sup> = 0 ⇒ y = 4. So 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x = 2.

questions.question: Solve: 2(x/(x + 1))<sup>2</sup> − 5(x/(x + 1)) + 2 = 0
questions.explanation: Let y = x/(x + 1): 2y<sup>2</sup> − 5y + 2 = 0 ⇒ (2y − 1)(y − 2) = 0 ⇒ y = 1/2 or y = 2. If y = 1/2: x/(x + 1) = 1/2 ⇒ 2x = x + 1 ⇒ x = 1. If y = 2: x/(x + 1) = 2 ⇒ x = 2x + 2 ⇒ x = −2.

questions.question: Solve: 4(x/(x − 1))<sup>2</sup> − 4(x/(x − 1)) + 1 = 0
questions.explanation: Let y = x/(x − 1): 4y<sup>2</sup> − 4y + 1 = 0 ⇒ (2y − 1)<sup>2</sup> = 0 ⇒ y = 1/2. So x/(x − 1) = 1/2 ⇒ 2x = x − 1 ⇒ x = −1.

questions.question: Solve: 9<sup>x + 2</sup> − 6·3<sup>x + 1</sup> + 1 = 0
questions.explanation: 9<sup>x + 2</sup> = 9<sup>2</sup>·9<sup>x</sup> = 81·3<sup>2x</sup> and 6·3<sup>x + 1</sup> = 18·3<sup>x</sup>. Let y = 3<sup>x</sup>: 81y<sup>2</sup> − 18y + 1 = 0 ⇒ (9y − 1)<sup>2</sup> = 0 ⇒ y = 1/9. So 3<sup>x</sup> = 3<sup>−2</sup> ⇒ x = −2.

questions.question: Solve: 2<sup>x</sup> + 2<sup>−x + 6</sup> − 20 = 0
questions.explanation: Write 2<sup>−x + 6</sup> = 64/2<sup>x</sup>. Let y = 2<sup>x</sup>: y + 64/y − 20 = 0 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> − 20y + 64 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 16) = 0 ⇒ y = 4 or y = 16. So 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x = 2, or 2<sup>x</sup> = 2<sup>4</sup> ⇒ x = 4.

questions.question: Solve: (x − 1)(x + 5)(x + 8)(x + 2) = 880
questions.explanation: Pair as [(x − 1)(x + 8)][(x + 5)(x + 2)] = 880 ⇒ (x<sup>2</sup> + 7x − 8)(x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 10) = 880. Let y = x<sup>2</sup> + 7x: (y − 8)(y + 10) = 880 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> + 2y − 960 = 0 ⇒ (y + 32)(y − 30) = 0 ⇒ y = 30 or y = −32. If x<sup>2</sup> + 7x = 30 ⇒ (x + 10)(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 3 or x = −10. If x<sup>2</sup> + 7x = −32 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> + 7x + 32 = 0 ⇒ x = (−7 ± √79 i)/2.

questions.question: Solve: (x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)(x + 4) = 120
questions.explanation: Pair as [(x + 1)(x + 4)][(x + 2)(x + 3)] = 120 ⇒ (x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 4)(x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 6) = 120. Let y = x<sup>2</sup> + 5x: (y + 4)(y + 6) = 120 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> + 10y − 96 = 0 ⇒ (y + 16)(y − 6) = 0 ⇒ y = 6 or y = −16. If x<sup>2</sup> + 5x = 6 ⇒ (x + 6)(x − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = 1 or x = −6. If x<sup>2</sup> + 5x = −16 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> + 5x + 16 = 0 ⇒ x = (−5 ± √39 i)/2.

questions.question: Solve: (x − 2)(x + 1)(x + 3)(x − 4) = 24
questions.explanation: Pair as [(x − 2)(x + 1)][(x + 3)(x − 4)] = 24 ⇒ (x<sup>2</sup> − x − 2)(x<sup>2</sup> − x − 12) = 24. Let y = x<sup>2</sup> − x: (y − 2)(y − 12) = 24 ⇒ y<sup>2</sup> − 14y = 0 ⇒ y(y − 14) = 0 ⇒ y = 0 or y = 14. If x<sup>2</sup> − x = 0 ⇒ x(x − 1) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 or x = 1. If x<sup>2</sup> − x = 14 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − x − 14 = 0 ⇒ x = (1 ± √57)/2.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: x + √(x + 5) = 7
questions.explanation: √(x + 5) = 7 − x. Squaring: x + 5 = 49 − 14x + x<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 15x + 44 = 0 ⇒ (x − 4)(x − 11) = 0 ⇒ x = 4 or x = 11. Checking, x = 11 does not satisfy the original (7 − x is negative), so x = 4.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: √(x − 2) = 8 − x
questions.explanation: Squaring: x − 2 = 64 − 16x + x<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 17x + 66 = 0 ⇒ (x − 6)(x − 11) = 0 ⇒ x = 6 or x = 11. Checking, x = 11 makes the right side negative, so x = 6.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: √(7 − 5x) + √(13 − 5x) = 3√(4 − 2x)
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides and simplifying gives 20 − 10x + 2√((7 − 5x)(13 − 5x)) = 36 − 18x ⇒ √((7 − 5x)(13 − 5x)) = 8 − 4x. Squaring again: (7 − 5x)(13 − 5x) = (8 − 4x)<sup>2</sup> ⇒ 91 − 100x + 25x<sup>2</sup> = 64 − 64x + 16x<sup>2</sup> ⇒ 9x<sup>2</sup> − 36x + 27 = 0 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> − 4x + 3 = 0 ⇒ (x − 1)(x − 3) = 0. Both x = 1 and x = 3 check.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: √(x + 2) + √(x + 7) = √(6x + 13)
questions.explanation: Squaring: 2x + 9 + 2√((x + 2)(x + 7)) = 6x + 13 ⇒ √((x + 2)(x + 7)) = 2x + 2. Squaring: (x + 2)(x + 7) = (2x + 2)<sup>2</sup> ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> + 9x + 14 = 4x<sup>2</sup> + 8x + 4 ⇒ 3x<sup>2</sup> − x − 10 = 0 ⇒ (3x + 5)(x − 2) = 0 ⇒ x = 2 or x = −5/3. Only x = 2 satisfies the original.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: √(2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 4) + √(2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x + 9) = 5
questions.explanation: Let t = 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x. Then √(t + 4) + √(t + 9) = 5. Squaring: (t + 4) + (t + 9) + 2√((t + 4)(t + 9)) = 25 ⇒ 2√((t + 4)(t + 9)) = 12 − 2t ⇒ √((t + 4)(t + 9)) = 6 − t. Squaring: (t + 4)(t + 9) = (6 − t)<sup>2</sup> ⇒ t<sup>2</sup> + 13t + 36 = 36 − 12t + t<sup>2</sup> ⇒ 25t = 0 ⇒ t = 0. So 2x<sup>2</sup> + 3x = 0 ⇒ x(2x + 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 or x = −3/2.

questions.question: Solve the radical equation: √(y<sup>2</sup> − 3y + 9) − √(y<sup>2</sup> − 3y + 36) + 3 = 0
questions.explanation: Let t = y<sup>2</sup> − 3y. Then √(t + 9) + 3 = √(t + 36). Squaring: (t + 9) + 6√(t + 9) + 9 = t + 36 ⇒ 6√(t + 9) = 18 ⇒ √(t + 9) = 3 ⇒ t + 9 = 9 ⇒ t = 0. So y<sup>2</sup> − 3y = 0 ⇒ y(y − 3) = 0 ⇒ y = 0 or y = 3.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: A polynomial equation in which degree of variable is ________ called quadratic equation.
questions.explanation: A quadratic equation is a polynomial equation in which the highest power (degree) of the variable is 2.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Standard form of quadratic equation is ________.
questions.explanation: The standard (general) form of a quadratic equation is ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 3<sup>x</sup> + 3<sup>2x</sup> = 1 is called a/an ________ equation.
questions.explanation: The unknown appears in the exponent, so the equation is an exponential equation.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Solution of 3<sup>x</sup> = 9 is ________.
questions.explanation: 3<sup>x</sup> = 9 = 3<sup>2</sup>, so x = 2.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Solution of ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0 is ________.
questions.explanation: For ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0, the roots are given by the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac))/2a.

questions.question: Degree of quadratic equation is:
questions.explanation: A quadratic equation has degree 2.

questions.question: Standard form of quadratic equation is:
questions.explanation: The standard form is ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
questions.optionsRaw: a) ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0  b) ax<sup>2</sup> + c = 0, a ≠ 0  c) ax<sup>2</sup> + bx = 0, a ≠ 0  d) ax<sup>3</sup> + bx<sup>2</sup> + c = 0, a ≠ 0

questions.question: The quadratic formula for ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0 is:
questions.explanation: The general quadratic formula is x = (−b ± √(b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac))/2a.
questions.optionsRaw: a) x = (−b − √(b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac))/2  b) x = (b ± √(b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac))/2a  c) x = (−b ± √(b<sup>2</sup> − 4ac))/2a  d) x = (−b ± √(b<sup>2</sup> + 4ac))/2a

questions.question: Solution set of x<sup>2</sup> + 10x + 24 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: x<sup>2</sup> + 10x + 24 = (x + 6)(x + 4) = 0 ⇒ x = −6 or x = −4.
questions.optionsRaw: a) {−6, −4}  b) {−6, 4}  c) {6, 4}  d) {6, −4}

questions.question: How many maximum roots of a quadratic equation are there?
questions.explanation: A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

questions.question: Two linear factors of x<sup>2</sup> − 15x + 56 are:
questions.explanation: (x − 7)(x − 8) = x<sup>2</sup> − 15x + 56.
questions.optionsRaw: a) (x − 7) and (x + 8)  b) (x + 7) and (x − 8)  c) (x − 7) and (x − 8)  d) (x + 7) and (x + 8)

questions.question: Polynomial equation which remains unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x is called a/an:
questions.explanation: A polynomial equation unchanged when x is replaced by 1/x is called a reciprocal equation.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Exponential equation  b) Reciprocal equation  c) Radical equation  d) none of these

questions.question: An equation of the type 3<sup>x</sup> + 3<sup>2 − x</sup> + 6 = 0 is a/an:
questions.explanation: The variable appears in the exponent, so it is an exponential equation.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Exponential equation  b) Radical equation  c) Reciprocal equation  d) none of these

questions.question: The solution set of equation 4x<sup>2</sup> − 16 = 0 is:
questions.explanation: 4x<sup>2</sup> = 16 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> = 4 ⇒ x = ±2.
questions.optionsRaw: a) {±4}  b) {4}  c) {±2}  d) none of these

questions.question: An equation of the form 2x<sup>4</sup> − 3x<sup>3</sup> + 7x<sup>2</sup> − 3x + 2 = 0 is called a/an:
questions.explanation: Replacing x by 1/x and clearing denominators gives the same equation, so it is a reciprocal equation.
questions.optionsRaw: a) Reciprocal equation  b) Radical equation  c) Exponential equation  d) none of these

questions.question: True or False: Every quadratic equation can be solved by factorization.
questions.explanation: Not every quadratic equation can be factorized over the reals (for example x<sup>2</sup> + 1 = 0), so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Every quartic equation has two roots.
questions.explanation: A quartic (degree 4) equation has four roots, not two.

questions.question: True or False: Every quadratic equation can have no solution.
questions.explanation: A quadratic equation may have real, equal, or complex roots; it is not the case that every quadratic has no solution.

questions.question: True or False: ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = 0 is called the quadratic equation in x if a = 0 and b, c are real numbers.
questions.explanation: For a quadratic equation we must have a ≠ 0; if a = 0 the equation is linear, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Extraneous roots satisfy the equation.
questions.explanation: Extraneous roots arise from squaring and do NOT satisfy the original equation, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Extraneous roots do not satisfy the equation.
questions.explanation: By definition an extraneous root does not satisfy the original equation.

questions.question: True or False: In the quadratic equation the highest exponent of the variable is two.
questions.explanation: A quadratic equation has degree 2, so the highest exponent of the variable is two.

questions.question: In the adjacent figure, m AB = m CB and ∠A ≅ ∠C. Prove that ΔABD ≅ ΔCBE.
questions.explanation: Proof: In ΔABD ↔ ΔCBE: (i) ∠A ≅ ∠C (given); (ii) AB ≅ CB (given); (iii) ∠ABD ≅ ∠CBE (vertically opposite angles). Hence ΔABD ≅ ΔCBE by the A.S.A. postulate. Q.E.D.

questions.question: From a point on the line bisector of an angle, perpendiculars are drawn to the arms of the angle. Prove that these perpendiculars are equal in measure.
questions.explanation: Given: OB bisects ∠AOC; P is a point on OB; PQ ⊥ OA and PR ⊥ OC. To prove: PQ ≅ PR. Proof: In ΔPOQ ↔ ΔPOR: (i) ∠PQO ≅ ∠PRO (= 90°, given); (ii) ∠POQ ≅ ∠POR (OB bisects ∠AOC); (iii) OP ≅ OP (common). Hence ΔPOQ ≅ ΔPOR by A.A.S., so PQ ≅ PR. Q.E.D.

questions.question: In the given figure, ΔACE ≅ ΔBDE, such that m∠A = (3x + 1)°, m∠B = (x + 35)°, m∠AEC = (3y − 2)° and m∠DEB = (y + 8)°. Find the values of x and y.
questions.explanation: Since ΔACE ≅ ΔBDE, corresponding angles are equal. ∠A = ∠B ⇒ 3x + 1 = x + 35 ⇒ 2x = 34 ⇒ x = 17. Also ∠AEC = ∠DEB ⇒ 3y − 2 = y + 8 ⇒ 2y = 10 ⇒ y = 5.

questions.question: In the given figure, ΔDEF ≅ ΔPQR, such that m DE = (6x + 1) cm, m EF = 8 cm, m RQ = (5y − 7) cm and m PQ = (10x − 19) cm. Find the values of x and y.
questions.explanation: In ΔDEF ↔ ΔPQR, DE ↔ PQ and EF ↔ QR. So 6x + 1 = 10x − 19 ⇒ 4x = 20 ⇒ x = 5. Also EF = QR ⇒ 8 = 5y − 7 ⇒ 5y = 15 ⇒ y = 3.

questions.question: ABC is a triangle in which m∠A = 35° and m∠B = 100°, BD ⊥ AC. Prove that ΔBDC is an isosceles triangle.
questions.explanation: Proof: In ΔABC, ∠C = 180° − (35° + 100°) = 45°. Since BD ⊥ AC, ∠BDC = 90°. In right ΔBDC, ∠DBC = 90° − ∠C = 90° − 45° = 45°. Thus ∠DBC ≅ ∠BCD (each 45°), so the sides opposite them are equal: DB ≅ DC. Hence ΔBDC is isosceles. Q.E.D.

questions.question: If the bisector of an angle of a triangle is perpendicular to its opposite side, then prove that triangle is an isosceles triangle.
questions.explanation: Given: In ΔABC, AD bisects ∠A and AD ⊥ BC. To prove: ΔABC is isosceles. Proof: In ΔADB ↔ ΔADC: (i) ∠BAD ≅ ∠DAC (AD bisects ∠A); (ii) ∠ADB ≅ ∠ADC (= 90°, AD ⊥ BC); (iii) AD ≅ AD (common). Hence ΔADB ≅ ΔADC by A.S.A., so AB ≅ AC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: ABC is a triangle in which m∠B = 45° and CD ⊥ AB. Prove that ΔDBC is an isosceles triangle.
questions.explanation: Proof: Since CD ⊥ AB, ∠BDC = 90°. In right ΔDBC, ∠B = 45°, so ∠BCD = 90° − 45° = 45°. Thus ∠B ≅ ∠BCD, so the opposite sides are equal: DB ≅ DC. Hence ΔDBC is isosceles. Q.E.D.

questions.question: ABC is an isosceles triangle. D is the mid-point of base BC. Prove that AD bisects ∠A and AD ⊥ BC.
questions.explanation: Proof: In ΔABD ↔ ΔACD: (i) AB ≅ AC (isosceles); (ii) BD ≅ DC (D is mid-point); (iii) AD ≅ AD (common). Hence ΔABD ≅ ΔACD by S.S.S. So ∠BAD ≅ ∠DAC (AD bisects ∠A) and ∠ADB ≅ ∠ADC. Since BD and DC are collinear, ∠ADB + ∠ADC = 180°; being equal, each is 90°. Hence AD ⊥ BC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: ABC and DBC are two isosceles triangles on the same side of a common base BC. Prove that AD is the right bisector of BC.
questions.answer: AD is the right bisector of BC.
questions.explanation: Proof: In isosceles ΔABC, AB ≅ AC, so A is equidistant from B and C and therefore lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC. In isosceles ΔDBC, DB ≅ DC, so D is also equidistant from B and C and lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC. Since A and D both lie on the perpendicular bisector of BC, the line AD is that perpendicular bisector, i.e. AD is the right bisector of BC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: PQRS is a square. X, Y and Z are the mid-points of PQ, QR and RS respectively. Prove that ΔPXY ≅ ΔSZY.
questions.explanation: Proof: Let the side of the square be a. Since X, Y, Z are mid-points: PX = ½a, SZ = ½a. In right ΔPQY, PY = √(a<sup>2</sup> + (½a)<sup>2</sup>) = ½a√5; likewise in right ΔSRY, SY = ½a√5, so PY ≅ SY. In right ΔQXY, XY = √((½a)<sup>2</sup> + (½a)<sup>2</sup>) = ½a√2; likewise in right ΔZRY, ZY = ½a√2, so XY ≅ ZY. Thus PX ≅ SZ, PY ≅ SY and XY ≅ ZY, giving ΔPXY ≅ ΔSZY by S.S.S. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that, in an equilateral triangle, any two medians are congruent.
questions.answer: Any two medians of an equilateral triangle are congruent.
questions.explanation: Proof: Let ABC be equilateral and let BM, CN be two medians (M mid-point of AC, N mid-point of AB). Then AB ≅ AC (equilateral), AM ≅ AN (halves of equal sides) and ∠BAM ≅ ∠CAN (the common angle A). Hence ΔBAM ≅ ΔCAN by S.A.S., so BM ≅ CN. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that the perpendiculars from the vertices of the base to opposite sides of an isosceles triangle are congruent.
questions.explanation: Given: ΔABC with AB ≅ AC; BE ⊥ AC and CF ⊥ AB. To prove: BE ≅ CF. Proof: In ΔBEC ↔ ΔCFB: (i) ∠BEC ≅ ∠CFB (= 90°); (ii) BC ≅ BC (common); (iii) ∠EBC ≅ ∠FCB (both equal 90° − base angle, and base angles are equal). Hence ΔBEC ≅ ΔCFB by A.A.S., so BE ≅ CF. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that, if the bisector of an angle of a triangle bisects its opposite side, then the triangle will be an isosceles triangle.
questions.explanation: Given: In ΔABC, AD bisects ∠A and BD ≅ DC. To prove: AB ≅ AC. Proof: Produce AD to E such that AD ≅ DE, and join C to E. In ΔADB ↔ ΔEDC: AD ≅ DE (construction), BD ≅ DC (given) and ∠ADB ≅ ∠EDC (vertically opposite). So ΔADB ≅ ΔEDC by S.A.S., giving AB ≅ EC and ∠BAD ≅ ∠CED. But ∠BAD ≅ ∠DAC (AD bisects ∠A), so ∠CED ≅ ∠DAC, i.e. ∠CEA ≅ ∠CAE. Hence AC ≅ CE. Therefore AB ≅ CE ≅ AC, i.e. AB ≅ AC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that the median bisecting the base of an isosceles triangle bisects the vertical angle and is perpendicular to the base.
questions.explanation: Given: ΔABC with AB ≅ AC and AD the median to base BC (BD ≅ DC). To prove: AD bisects ∠A and AD ⊥ BC. Proof: In ΔABD ↔ ΔACD: AB ≅ AC (given), BD ≅ DC (given), AD ≅ AD (common). Hence ΔABD ≅ ΔACD by S.S.S. So ∠BAD ≅ ∠DAC (AD bisects ∠A) and ∠ADB ≅ ∠ADC. Since ∠ADB + ∠ADC = 180° and they are equal, each equals 90°; hence AD ⊥ BC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that if three altitudes of a triangle are congruent, then the triangle is equilateral.
questions.explanation: Given: ΔABC with altitudes AD ⊥ BC, BE ⊥ CA, CF ⊥ AB such that AD ≅ BE ≅ CF. Proof: The area of ΔABC computed from each base is equal: ½(BC)(AD) = ½(CA)(BE) = ½(AB)(CF). Since AD ≅ BE ≅ CF, the products being equal forces BC ≅ CA ≅ AB. Hence the triangle is equilateral. Q.E.D.

questions.question: If ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, m∠F is equal to (from the figure m∠A = 120° and m∠B = 30°):
questions.explanation: In ΔABC, m∠C = 180° − (120° + 30°) = 30°. Since ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF, ∠F corresponds to ∠C, so m∠F = 30°.
questions.optionsRaw: a) 90°  b) 60°  c) 30°  d) 20°

questions.question: True or False: The sum of the measures of all angles in a quadrilateral is 360°.
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral can be divided into two triangles, so the sum of its angles is 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.question: True or False: The sum of the measures of all angles in a triangle is 270°.
questions.explanation: The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°, not 270°.

questions.question: True or False: In an equilateral triangle, angles are of the same measurement.
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle is equiangular; all three angles equal 60°.

questions.question: True or False: There are two right angles in a triangle.
questions.explanation: A triangle can have at most one right angle, since the sum of the angles is only 180°.

questions.question: True or False: In an isosceles triangle, corresponding angles and corresponding sides are equal in measure.
questions.explanation: In an isosceles triangle only the two base angles are equal and the two legs (opposite them) are equal; not every corresponding angle and side is equal.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: If ΔABC ↔ ΔDEF, then AC corresponds to ________.
questions.explanation: In the correspondence ΔABC ↔ ΔDEF, the orders are A↔D, B↔E, C↔F, so side AC corresponds to side DF.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In ΔKLM ↔ ΔPQR, then ∠MKL corresponds to ________.
questions.explanation: In ΔKLM ↔ ΔPQR we have K↔P, L↔Q, M↔R. The angle MKL (at K) corresponds to the angle RPQ (at P).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In an isosceles triangle, the base angles are ________.
questions.explanation: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal in measure.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: If the measure of each angle of a triangle is 60°, then the triangle is ________.
questions.explanation: If all three angles are 60°, all three sides are equal, so the triangle is equilateral.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite to the right angle is called the ________.
questions.explanation: The side opposite the right angle in a right-angled triangle is the hypotenuse.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The sum of the measures of the acute angles of a right triangle is ________.
questions.explanation: In a right triangle one angle is 90°, so the two acute angles sum to 180° − 90° = 90°.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sufficient condition for congruence of two triangles?
questions.explanation: A.A.A (Angle-Angle-Angle) guarantees only similarity, not congruence, because equal angles do not fix the size of the triangles. Without a pair of corresponding equal sides, the triangles need not be congruent.
questions.optionsRaw: a) A.S.A ≅ A.S.A  b) H.S ≅ H.S  c) S.A.A ≅ S.A.A  d) A.A.A ≅ A.A.A

questions.question: In ΔABC, if ∠A ≅ ∠B, then the bisector of the ________ angle divides the triangle into two congruent triangles.
questions.explanation: Since ∠A ≅ ∠B, the sides opposite them are equal (CA ≅ CB). The bisector of the vertical angle ∠C divides the isosceles ΔABC into two congruent triangles (by S.A.S.).
questions.optionsRaw: a) ∠A  b) ∠B  c) ∠C  d) any one of its angles

questions.question: The diagonal of a ________ does not divide it into two congruent triangles.
questions.explanation: A diagonal of a rectangle, parallelogram or square divides it into two congruent triangles, but a diagonal of a trapezium does not (the two triangles formed are not congruent in general).
questions.optionsRaw: a) Rectangle  b) Trapezium  c) Parallelogram  d) Square

questions.question: How many acute angles are there in an acute-angled triangle?
questions.explanation: In an acute-angled triangle all three angles are acute, so there are 3 acute angles.
questions.optionsRaw: a) 1  b) 2  c) 3  d) not more than 2

questions.question: Prove that the line joining the mid-points of two opposite sides of a parallelogram is parallel to the other sides.
questions.answer: The joining line is parallel to the other two sides.
questions.explanation: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram; M and N are the mid-points of AB and CD. To prove: MN ∥ AD ∥ BC. Proof: AM = ½AB = ½CD = DN, and AB ∥ CD so AM ∥ DN. Hence AMND has one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel, so it is a parallelogram. Therefore MN ∥ AD. Since AD ∥ BC, we get MN ∥ AD ∥ BC. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that interior angles on any side of a parallelogram are supplementary.
questions.answer: Each pair of interior angles on the same side is supplementary.
questions.explanation: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram. To prove: ∠A + ∠B = 180° (and likewise ∠B + ∠C = 180°, etc.). Proof: AD ∥ BC with AB as transversal, so the interior angles on the same side are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180°. Similarly AB ∥ CD with BC as transversal gives ∠B + ∠C = 180°, and so on. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that the bisectors of two angles on the same side of a parallelogram cut each other at right angle.
questions.explanation: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram; the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at P. To prove: ∠APB = 90°. Proof: Since interior angles on the same side are supplementary, ∠A + ∠B = 180°. Also ∠PAB = ½∠A and ∠PBA = ½∠B. In ΔAPB: ∠APB = 180° − (∠PAB + ∠PBA) = 180° − ½(∠A + ∠B) = 180° − 90° = 90°. Q.E.D.

questions.question: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then prove that it is a parallelogram.
questions.explanation: Given: Quadrilateral ABCD whose diagonals AC and BD bisect each other at O (AO ≅ OC, BO ≅ OD). To prove: ABCD is a parallelogram. Proof: In ΔAOB ↔ ΔCOD: AO ≅ OC (given), BO ≅ OD (given) and ∠AOB ≅ ∠COD (vertically opposite). So ΔAOB ≅ ΔCOD (S.A.S.), giving ∠OAB ≅ ∠OCD, which are alternate angles ⇒ AB ∥ CD. Similarly ΔAOD ≅ ΔCOB gives AD ∥ BC. Hence ABCD is a parallelogram. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that in a parallelogram opposite angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram. To prove: ∠A ≅ ∠C and ∠B ≅ ∠D. Proof: Consecutive angles are supplementary: ∠A + ∠B = 180° and ∠C + ∠B = 180°. Hence ∠A = 180° − ∠B = ∠C, so ∠A ≅ ∠C. Similarly ∠B = 180° − ∠A = ∠D, so ∠B ≅ ∠D. Q.E.D.

questions.question: Prove that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram if its opposite angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: Given: Quadrilateral ABCD with ∠A ≅ ∠C and ∠B ≅ ∠D. To prove: ABCD is a parallelogram. Proof: The sum of the angles is 360°, so ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360° ⇒ 2∠A + 2∠B = 360° ⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 180°. These are consecutive interior angles, so AD ∥ BC. Similarly ∠B + ∠C = 180° gives AB ∥ CD. Hence ABCD is a parallelogram. Q.E.D.
